# Greece — English books

**GREECE OPENED 2026-11-03 under the user's all-closed-countries
ruling.** Greece is CLOSED in the library. Its English set as
recorded is 62 files — Grades 1–12: 48 student-side (incl.
workbooks) + 14 teacher. Of those, **43 files are in hand and
43 are read and filed below**; **19 are link-only** (exact
source links recorded, files not yet held — mostly primary
teacher guides/workbooks and older-edition primary books, plus
three Grade 12 cross-reference rows whose books are the Grade
11 files read under Grade 11). The link-only books enter this
file when their files land; they are listed at the end.

Almost all books are ITYE «Diophantos» (Institute of Computer
Technology and Publications) books for the Greek Ministry of
Education, from the ministry's ebooks.edu.gr platform. The
exceptions, each flagged in its section: the three maritime
books (Maritime English Volumes 1–2 and the IMO Standard
Marine Communication Phrases) are **Eugenides Foundation**
books written for the Merchant Navy Academies and adopted
into the EPAL lists under Diophantos codes; and two EPAL
teacher's books are held in their original **OEDB** printings
rather than the Diophantos reissues (corrections 4–5). The
primary series runs Alpha English (G1) and Beta English (G2)
— whose held pupil files are the print **Workpack** artwork
packs (see the record corrections) — then Αγγλικά for G3–G6
(G3's Magic Book set is link-only; the held G4–G6 books are
the Revised Edition pupil's books). Gymnasio (G7–G8) runs two
streams, Advanced (Προχωρημένοι) and Beginners (Αρχάριοι),
both titled *Think Teen!*; G9 has a single-stream set. Lykeio
(G10–G12) has the general Αγγλικά line plus EPAL vocational
English (sector English, Maritime English, office/hotel
specialisms).

## Grade 1 — ALPHA ENGLISH, Student's Book — ⚠ IDENTITY MISMATCH: this file is the WORKPACK, not the Student's Book

Real title as printed (front cover, PDF p. 1 and back cover, PDF p. 145): **AlphaEnglish for 1st grade pupils — WORKPACK** (letter "A" volume).

Record title it was filed under: "ALPHA ENGLISH - Vivlio Mathiti (Student Book)", Greece Grade 1 (A' Dimotikou). **Verdict: MISMATCH.** The PDF is the print-ready artwork pack that accompanies Alpha English A — covers plus cut-out cards, flashcards and colouring sheets — not the pupil's lesson book. No unit-by-unit lesson summary or language teaching can be filed from this file, and none is invented below. What follows is the verified identity of the file actually held, an inventory of what it does contain, and spot-verified anchors for that real content.

### Identity block

- **Title as printed:** AlphaEnglish for 1st grade pupils — WORKPACK
- **Series / level:** Alpha English "A", for 1st grade pupils (A' Dimotikou)
- **Publisher / imprint:** ΙΝΣΤΙΤΟΥΤΟ ΤΕΧΝΟΛΟΓΙΑΣ ΥΠΟΛΟΓΙΣΤΩΝ ΚΑΙ ΕΚΔΟΣΕΩΝ «ΔΙΟΦΑΝΤΟΣ» (ITYE "Diophantos"), for the Ministry of Education, Research and Religions (ΥΠΟΥΡΓΕΙΟ ΠΑΙΔΕΙΑΣ, ΕΡΕΥΝΑΣ ΚΑΙ ΘΡΗΣΚΕΥΜΑΤΩΝ) and the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (ΕΘΝΙΚΟ ΚΑΙ ΚΑΠΟΔΙΣΤΡΙΑΚΟ ΠΑΝΕΠΙΣΤΗΜΙΟ ΑΘΗΝΩΝ)
- **Project:** "Learning English in Early Childhood" (Η ΕΚΜΑΘΣΗ ΤΗΣ ΑΓΓΛΙΚΗΣ ΣΕ ΠΡΩΙΜΗ ΠΑΙΔΙΚΗ ΗΛΙΚΙΑ), ESPA 2007–2013 co-funded; scientific lead Vasiliki Dendrinou (Βασιλική Δενδρινού); writing team headed by Katerina Nikolaki, with Alexia Giannakopoulou, Klairi Kosovitsa-Varela and Maria Bouzouki (credits page, PDF p. 3)
- **Edition / year as printed:** No edition statement or year is printed on the cover or credits page. The print files are dated 1/4/2014 in the production slugs (e.g. "A_COVER_59x35.indd 1, 1/4/2014"); PDF producer metadata: Adobe InDesign CS4, created 1 Apr 2014, modified 15 Sep 2020. Treat 2014 as the print-file date, not a printed edition date.
- **Book code as printed (back cover, PDF p. 145):** Κωδικός βιβλίου: 0-10-0186
- **ISBN as printed (back cover, PDF p. 145):** ISBN 978-960-06-4460-9 — barcode (01) 000000 0 10 0186 0
- **PDF pages:** 145
- **Printed page numbers / offset:** **None — no printed folios exist anywhere in this file, so no printed = PDF offset can be given.** Interior sheets carry only production codes (see below) and the InDesign slug "A_ARTWORK_PRINT.indd N", where for the interior PDF p. = indd N + 2 (e.g. PDF p. 9 = indd 7; PDF p. 120 = indd 118). All page references in this section are therefore PDF pages plus artwork codes.
- **File structure:** PDF p. 1 = cover spread (front cover, right half); p. 2 = inside-cover / copyright sheet (repeated at p. 144); p. 3 = title and credits page; pp. 4–143 = artwork sheets; p. 145 = cover spread repeated, showing the back cover with ISBN (left half).

### What the file actually contains — artwork inventory (own words)

Every interior sheet is a full-bleed print sheet with crop marks and colour bars, carrying pictures to cut out and use in class. There is no running text, no lesson, no dialogue, no instructions to pupils, and (with the exception of the environmental-print sheet, PDF p. 4) the pictures carry no English words at all — the vocabulary exists only as images. Sheets are coded `A_<section><unit>_<type><number>`: sections Α, Β, Γ (Gamma), Δ (Delta) and Ε; types C = cut-out card/picture pieces, F = flashcards, W = worksheet/colouring artwork, S = a make-it sheet (one only).

- **Section Α — opening set, PDF pp. 4–8 (codes A_A00–A_A03):** One environmental-print collage sheet (A_A00_C01, p. 4) showing English words as found on signs and objects around a Greek child — shop, road and safety signs and a puzzle box — with the course's bear mascot in a smiley-face shirt. Then three small card sets and two 4-picture flashcard sheets (A_A03_F01–F08, pp. 7–8).
- **Section Β — ten units, PDF pp. 9–45 (codes A_B01–A_B10):** The largest early block. It opens with animal picture flashcards with no words printed on them — six pet/zoo-type animals per sheet (A_B01_F01–F06, p. 9) — followed by matching black-and-white colour-and-cut versions of the same animals (A_B01_W01–W02, pp. 10–11). Unit B02 adds a fold-up animal dice net (A_B02_S01, p. 14) showing six animals. Unit B06 is a long run of nine worksheet-artwork sheets (A_B06_W01–W09, pp. 23–31); B07 is the biggest flashcard run, eighteen cards over three sheets (A_B07_F01–F18, pp. 32–34); B10 closes the section with seven card sheets and a worksheet (pp. 41–45).
- **Section Γ — ten units, PDF pp. 46–85 (codes A_Γ01–A_Γ10):** Opens with a build-a-face cut-out (A_Γ01_C01, p. 46): a cartoon monkey head with separate loose eyes, nose, mouth and ears to place on it — body-part/face artwork in picture form only. The section is card-heavy; its Γ09 set includes nature and seasons flashcards (A_Γ09_F07–F12, p. 80 indd 78): a bare winter tree, grey clouds, snowflakes, a leafy summer tree, a smiling sun and coloured flowers, again with no words on the cards.
- **Section Δ — six units, PDF pp. 86–115 (codes A_Δ01–A_Δ06):** A shorter block mixing card sheets and worksheet artwork (e.g. A_Δ02_W02, p. 91; A_Δ06_C08-9, p. 111). Same format throughout: pictures only, production-coded, unpaginated.
- **Section Ε — six units, PDF pp. 116–143 (codes A_E01–A_E06):** The closing block. It includes large outline artwork for colouring/making, e.g. an owl-like mask outline (A_E01_W01, p. 120), three card sheets for E04 (pp. 134–138 grouping A_E04_C02-3, C04-5, C06, C07), and a final six-flashcard sheet (A_E06_F01–F06, p. 143).
- **Totals from the production codes:** roughly 75 C (card/cut-out) items, 108 F (flashcard) items, 48 W (worksheet-artwork) items and 1 S (dice/make-it) item are coded across the 140 interior sheets — counts are of code occurrences including group-range labels, so they are approximate, and every item is artwork, not text.

### Honest negatives — what cannot be taken from this file

- This file teaches nothing in text form: it contains **no lessons, units, dialogues, songs, chants, stories, grammar, reading passages or pupil instructions** — so no claim about what Grade 1 pupils learn (vocabulary sets, language points, tenses or otherwise) can be sourced to it. In particular it is not evidence for the presence *or* absence of any language point (e.g. past tense) in the Alpha English course; that judgement must wait for the real Student's Book.
- It has **no printed page numbers**, no contents page and no unit titles; the Α–Ε / 01–10 structure above is reconstructed from production codes only.
- The only English words in the whole interior are the environmental-print items on a single sheet (PDF p. 4, anchors 7–14 above); all flashcards and cards are wordless pictures.
- No audio, song lyrics or chant texts are printed anywhere in the file, although the credits page (PDF p. 3) lists music editors and voice speakers for separate audio files that are not included here.

### Filing note / next step

The catalogue code stem 10-0186 is shared with the Grade 1 Alpha English listing, which is the likely cause of the mix-up: the manifest record for this item points at the ebooks.edu.gr "Vivlio-Mathiti" viewer for 10-0186, but the file delivered under it is the Workpack print file (ISBN 978-960-06-4460-9, code 0-10-0186). **The real ALPHA ENGLISH Vivlio Mathiti (Student's Book) for Grade 1 still needs to be grabbed and read; this Workpack should be re-filed as a supplementary artwork pack, not counted as the Grade 1 student book.**
## Grade 2 — BETA ENGLISH, Student's Book (BetaEnglish for 2nd grade pupils — WORKPACK)

### Identity block

- **⚠ KIND MISMATCH — read first:** The record calls this the "Student Book" (Vivlio Mathiti). The book itself is **not** a conventional paginated student's book. Its cover (PDF p.1) and back cover (PDF p.197) both name it **"BetaEnglish for 2nd grade pupils — WORKPACK"**. It is a print-production file of loose classroom material — big picture cards, flashcard sheets, cut-out/colour/trace worksheets — with printer's crop marks, colour bars and InDesign file names ("B_ARTWORK_PRINT.indd …", dated 1/4/2014) printed on almost every sheet. Grade, subject, series, publisher and book code all match the record exactly, and this same code (10-0187) is the file ebooks.edu.gr serves as the Grade 2 pupil book; the Grade 1 Alpha book in the same programme is built the same way. Verdict: **the right book, in workpack form — not a wrong book, and not a textbook with lessons on numbered pages.**
- **Title as printed:** BetaEnglish (cover also "Beta English" on the credits page, PDF p.3)
- **Level:** for 2nd grade pupils (Β΄ Δημοτικού), English
- **Publisher / issuing bodies as printed:** Ministry of Education, Research and Religious Affairs (Υπουργείο Παιδείας, Έρευνας και Θρησκευμάτων) and the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens; publisher named at the foot of the credits page: ΙΤΥΕ «Διόφαντος» (Institute of Computer Technology and Publications "Diophantos"). Produced under the university's early-English project ("Learning English at an early childhood age", ESPA 2007–2013) — credits, PDF p.3.
- **Scientific lead / authors as printed (PDF p.3):** project lead Vasiliki Dendrinou, Professor, University of Athens; writing team headed by Evangelia Karagianni, with Fotini Veneti, Klairi Kosvitsa-Varela (also pedagogical adviser/co-ordinator), Amalia Balourdi, Melpomeni Barambouti, Dora Simsa.
- **Edition / year as printed:** no edition statement or year is printed on the cover or credits page. The print files are dated 1/4/2014 on the sheets; PDF metadata: created 1 April 2014, modified 15 September 2020.
- **ISBN as printed (cover/back cover):** ISBN 978-960-06-4458-6; book code 0-10-0187.
- **PDF pages:** 197.
- **Printed-page vs PDF-page offset:** **there are no printed page numbers (folios) anywhere in this book** — it is a pack of separate sheets, so no folio offset exists. The only pagination is the printer's artwork pagination: PDF pp.1–2 = cover spread and inside cover, PDF p.3 = credits (= artwork p.1), content sheets PDF pp.4–194 = artwork pp.2–192, audio contents PDF p.195 = artwork p.193, PDF pp.196–197 repeat the inside cover and cover. So for the content sheets, **artwork page = PDF page − 2**. All references below are PDF pages, with the sheet code printed on each sheet (e.g. B_B02_F01-6).
- **How the pack is organised:** five cycles (Κύκλοι) lettered A, B, Γ (Gamma), Δ (Delta), E. Each lesson's material is coded: **_C = big picture/story card, _F = flashcard sheet, _W = worksheet, _M = audio track (audio itself is not in this PDF)**. A contents list of the audio (PDF p.195) names every lesson's song/story and is the pack's own map. An alphabet strand runs through the whole book: one letter card + one tracing worksheet per letter, all 26 letters, in a non-alphabetical order, each with a short rhyme. The recurring characters are two bear cubs, Mary and Terry. Almost nothing in the pack carries printed instructions — it is teacher-led material used with the audio.

### Unit-by-unit summary (in my own words)

#### Cycle A — first meetings, feelings, numbers (PDF pp.4–22)

- **A01 — Meeting Mary and Terry (pp.4–6).** Two large character cards introduce the bear cubs with a greeting and their names; the worksheet is an outline head of each cub to colour/cut (a mask-like craft). Language: greeting + "I'm …" self-introduction.
- **A02 — Where is…? (pp.7–8).** Tall guessing cards show animals half-hidden (bird, zebra, dog, fish, lion, elephant, tiger, monkey, then pig, cow/horse, parrot, hippo, mouse, chick, turtle, cat). Zoo/farm animal vocabulary and a where-is-it guessing routine; the detail is in the audio track of the same name (PDF p.195).
- **A03 — Plate Sail (p.15 only).** One sheet of four blank mini-booklet templates (a dotted writing line facing a blank drawing box). Pupils make their own little word-and-picture booklets; the lesson's chant exists only as audio (PDF p.195).
- **A04 — Hello! How are you? / If you're happy (p.18).** Four feeling-face flashcards: happy, sad, unwell/tired and hungry are pictured (one face weeping, one yawning in bed, one with bib and cutlery). Feelings vocabulary, with the greeting question practised in the audio.
- **A05 — How old are you? (pp.19–20).** A caterpillar craft: colour ten body segments printed with the number words one–ten and glue the finished caterpillar in a notebook — numbers 1–10 as words. The second worksheet is a read-and-colour task: numbered shapes, each assigned a colour in a written list running from "Number 1" to "Number 10" — numbers 1–10 plus colour words yellow, blue, purple, green, black, red, grey, brown, orange, pink.
- **A06 — I am special (pp.21–22).** Food-counting flashcards pair quantities with single food items or groups (one cake, one pizza, three burgers, six biscuits, four bananas, eight carrots) — counting food. The worksheet is a first self-profile: a big blank head/face space with three started lines for the pupil's greeting, name/age word and a "I like …" line — likes and self-description.

*Alphabet strand in Cycle A:* Z zebra (pp.9–10), C cat (pp.11–12), L lion (pp.13–14), N name (pp.16–17) — each: letter shape, one key word, stroke-order tracing, and a 3–4 line rhyme (the N rhyme is about a girl whose name is Anna and who has a banana, contrasted with Lana).

#### Cycle B — school, home, body, animals, food, seasons (PDF pp.23–78)

- **B01 — The family (p.23 only).** One framed "photo" card of the bear family of five — father, mother, Mary, Terry and a baby. Family members, presented pictorially; B01 has no audio track in the contents list.
- **B02 — School objects (pp.26–29).** Sixteen picture flashcards of classroom things (schoolbag, pencil case, sharpener, copybook, pen, waste-paper bin, rubber, book, pencil, ruler), the last cards grouping them as plurals. The worksheet gives six dotted words to trace (ruler, bag, pencil, pen, bin, book) beside deliberately shuffled pictures to match. Singular/plural and naming classroom objects.
- **B03 — Toys (pp.32–33).** Flashcards: robot, doll, car, dinosaur, kite, yo-yo. The worksheet is a class-survey grid — names across the top, five toys down the side (a robot, a doll, a ball, a dinosaur, a kite) — for asking classmates about their toys.
- **B04 — Rooms of the house (pp.38–39).** A six-panel picture card of rooms (two bedrooms, kitchen, bathroom, dining room, living room) and an outline version of the same six rooms with blank label spaces. Rooms/furniture by picture; B04 has no audio track listed.
- **B05 — My bedroom: listen and check (pp.42–43).** A listening grid crosses two children's faces with six furniture pictures (bed, desk, lamp, computer, carpet, poster) to tick while listening. The second worksheet matches furniture pictures to six shuffled dotted words (bed, carpet, desk, poster, chair, lamp). Bedroom furniture.
- **B06 — Head & shoulders / Pinocchio's body (pp.44–45).** A full-body Pinocchio card in colour and the same figure in outline to colour. Body parts are carried by the two audio songs (a head-and-shoulders action song and an "If you are…" song, PDF p.195).
- **B07 — The Hokey Pokey (no printed sheet).** Movement/body lesson that exists only as an audio track (PDF p.195); nothing to file from the PDF itself.
- **B08 — Pets (p.48).** A "Pet Show" poster crowded with animals — horses, a bear, a dog, ducks/chicks, parrots, a squirrel, a cat, rabbits, a pig, a mouse. Pet/animal vocabulary supporting the audio "I've got a lot of pets"; have-got for pets.
- **B09 — Can it jump? (pp.49–51).** A card of four people of different ages/abilities (a baby, a basketball player, an elderly woman, a tennis player in a wheelchair); animal flashcards (eagle, dolphin, monkey, tiger, elephant, kangaroo); and an outline sheet of storybook characters. The audio pair (a walking/action song and "Can an elephant jump?") makes this the can/can't ability lesson, sorted by what each animal/person does.
- **B10 — Listen and number: monsters (p.56 only).** Three multi-eyed, multi-legged monsters to number in the order heard — counting body features (eyes, heads, legs) by listening.
- **B11 — The friendly ghost (pp.57–58).** Two big friendly ghosts to colour and a sheet of six ghost faces with different expressions. A story/song lesson (audio only for the words); ghost faces recycle the feelings set.
- **B12 — Numbers 1–20 (p.59 only).** A dense counting worksheet: mixed columns of butterflies, dinosaurs, cats, elephants, dolls, bats and baskets, each column headed by a dotted space for its counted total and the plural word. Counting up to about twenty, plural nouns; the audio adds a counting song and an explicit "Numbers 1–20" track.
- **B13 — Food and eating well (pp.60–64).** A food-wheel card and a labelled food-pyramid card (fats/oils/sweets at the top; milk group; meat-or-alternative group; vegetable group; fruit group; breads & cereals group at the base, marked as the "6 or more servings" group). Eighteen food flashcards: apple, chicken, bread, banana, cake, sweets, milk, cereal, meat, egg, fish, ice-cream, water, olive oil, juice, chips, salad, spaghetti. Food vocabulary sorted into healthy-eating groups; the audio is "An apple a day".
- **B14 — Seasons and the friendly snowman (pp.71–76).** A four-seasons picture card (summer beach things, winter snowman scene, spring flowers/butterfly, autumn leaves/umbrella), big cut-outs of a winter-dressed girl and a snowman, then thirteen flashcards sorting things by season: scarf, umbrella, flippers, ice cream, autumn leaf, gloves, butterfly, flower, and the girl snowboarding, skiing, ice-skating, dancing in snow and building the snowman. The closing worksheet is a snowman face to colour. Seasons, weather clothes and winter activities.

*Alphabet strand in Cycle B:* B bear (pp.24–25, rhyme about the bear family, big/tall), P pen (pp.30–31, a pen in a bag, pink), K kite (pp.34–35), Y yo-yo (pp.36–37), R rat (pp.40–41, "there's a rat in the room" — also drills in/on location), H hat (pp.46–47, hats on a head and on a bed), M monkey (pp.52–53, two girls taking a toy monkey and donkey to school), T tiger (pp.54–55), A apple (pp.65–66), F fish (pp.67–68, small fish vs big-and-tall owner), W water (pp.69–70), U umbrella (pp.77–78, an uncle at the seaside with a red umbrella).

#### Cycle Γ (Gamma) — time, jobs, transport, play, weather, the year (PDF pp.79–117)

- **Γ01 — Days of the week (pp.79–80).** A poster where snowmen act out a body action for each day (toe-tapping Sunday through sitting-down Saturday), and a tracing sheet of the seven day-names as cut-out cards. Day names plus action verbs (tap, rub, spin, touch, stamp, take a seat).
- **Γ02 — Mary's day and the clock (pp.81–85).** Nine story cards follow Mary through a day, each with an o'clock clock face: waking at 7, school at 8, lessons at 10, home at 2, eating at 3, reading at 4, playing at 6, shower at 8, bed at 9 (the small-card sheet, pp.83–85 order varies). Worksheets: number the nine day-pictures in order, and read-and-match scenes to "in the morning / in the afternoon / in the evening / at night". Daily routine, o'clock times, parts of the day. Γ02 has no audio track listed.
- **Γ03 — Jobs (pp.88–90).** Two story cards show tiny bear workers of many trades helping a big sick man (and the same man recovered) — a spot-the-jobs scene. Ten job flashcards, the cubs in costume: hairdresser, cook, dentist, doctor, farmer, plumber, police officer, teacher, builder, tailor. Jobs vocabulary; "Jobs" is the audio story/song.
- **Γ04 — Transport (pp.91–94).** A scene card grouping car, train, plane, ship and sailing boat; a photo card of transport around the world (a London double-decker bus, a dog sled, city cyclists, a man leading a laden animal); six vehicle flashcards (van, car, train, plane, boat, ship) and an outline cut-out set of the same six. Vehicles by land, sea and air; the audio is "The wheels on the bus".
- **Γ05 — More ways to travel (pp.97–99).** Nine more vehicle flashcards (hot-air balloon, bicycle, bus, donkey, helicopter, horse, motorbike, underground train, magic carpet) and a listening-choice worksheet pairing near-matches (train/metro, plane/helicopter, ship/boat, horse/donkey, bus/car, carpet/balloon, bicycle/motorbike) under the journey song "Over the mountains". Telling similar vehicles apart.
- **Γ06 — Clothes (p.100 only).** A two-panel spot/match sheet of clothing items — trousers, socks, trainers, T-shirt, shirt-and-tie, hat, dress, hooded jacket (the shirt, hat, trousers and socks repeat between panels). Clothes vocabulary by picture only. Γ06 has no audio track listed.
- **Γ07 — Playing in the playground: what are you doing? (pp.103–107).** An empty-playground scene (slide, climbing frame, roundabout, seesaw, swings, basketball hoop), then six flashcards of animals at play — a cat doing taekwondo, a bear playing football, a duck playing basketball, rabbits playing chess, a mouse doing ballet, a crocodile playing tennis. Three worksheets repeat those scenes with traced captions in the pattern "I'm playing …" / "I'm doing …" (chess, ballet, tennis, taekwondo, basketball, football). Present-continuous play activities, play/do contrast.
- **Γ08 — Weather (pp.108–110).** Four weather flashcards (snowy snowman, cloudy, windy, sunny); a sheet of four identical houses to draw a different weather/season scene on each; and a matching sheet linking three weather circles (rain, snow, sun) to the right clothes and gear (shorts, woolly hat, raincoat, umbrella, sunglasses, gloves, flip-flops). Weather words and dressing for the weather; audio "Rain, rain".
- **Γ09 — Happy birthday: seasons and months (pp.111–115).** A blank train engine and carriage to build a birthday/season train, then four colour-and-cut banners that name the seasons with their months in seasonal pictures: Spring (March, April, May), Summer (June, July, August), Autumn (September, October, November), Winter (December, January, February). Months of the year grouped by season; audio "Happy birthday" and "The season chant".

*Alphabet strand in Cycle Γ:* O o'clock (pp.86–87, a rock-around-the-clock counting chant, 1.00–6.00 o'clock), V van (pp.95–96, a man with a violin in a van), S socks (pp.101–102, whose socks are red/blue/purple — possessive 's in the rhyme), Q queen (pp.116–117, a quiet queen in a violet dress).

#### Cycle Δ (Delta) — stories: greetings, feelings, and five tales (PDF pp.118–165)

- **Δ01 — Mary's day: greetings through the day (pp.118–124).** Twelve story cards walk Mary from waking (alarm clock), washing/combing/dressing and a family breakfast with good-morning exchanges, to goodbye at the school gate, the teacher's good morning, the teacher's goodbye to the class at 1 o'clock, hello to mum at home, an afternoon of eating, reading, playing and television, and good-night exchanges at bedtime, ending asleep at 8. One worksheet matches traced greetings ("Good night / Goodbye / Good morning") to three of the scenes. Time-of-day greetings in a full-day story.
- **Δ02 — My new book: how are you today? Why? Because… (pp.125–130).** Six paired dialogue cards, all built the same way — a feeling on top, its reason below: happy because he has a new book; sad because his dog is sick; hungry because he left his sandwich at home; thirsty because he played basketball; angry because "we" lost the game (scoreboard 10–40); sleepy because he is tired. Feelings extended (adding thirsty, angry, sleepy) and because-reasons. The lesson's second audio track is another version of the happy-and-you-know-it song.
- **Δ03 — The selfish and greedy hippo (pp.131–132).** One riverside story card: a cow, a cat with cheese, a dog with chips and the hippo in the water eyeing everyone's food. Four animal-face masks (hippo, cow, cat, dog) to cut out and act the story. A greed/sharing moral tale told in audio; the printed side is props only.
- **Δ04 — The story of the rainbow (pp.135–138).** A large figure in Native American dress (the story's narrator figure), then small colour-character cards that speak for themselves in short lines: green is a tree and a leaf, blue is the sea and the sky, yellow is a sunflower, orange is the sunset, red is the fire, purple is a strong king — and all join to make a rainbow. The worksheet traces the six "I'm (colour)" captions under outline versions. Colour words tied to nature; the audio also offers a simplified version of the story and two classical-music listening tracks (Swan Lake; The Four Seasons).
- **Δ05 — Pinocchio (pp.141–144).** Five story cards: Geppetto carving the puppet; the fairy giving it life while Geppetto sleeps; the long-nosed puppet with donkey ears in a cage visited by the fairy; Geppetto inside the whale in a little boat while Pinocchio waits on a raft; and the happy ending outside the house with the whale behind them. The worksheet (p.144) is the book's longest printed text: a simplified retelling of the whole tale with picture gaps — the pupil cuts out the small pictures below (raft, house, sea, school, wand, puppet, boat, Geppetto, whale, fire, fairy) and glues each into its gap. Story sequencing and story vocabulary; told in the first person by Pinocchio at the end ("I am a real boy").
- **Δ06 — Grumpy Dog goes to a party (pp.145–149).** Eleven hand-drawn story cards with no words except the invitation itself: a grumpy dog at home (party clothes on the bed, card on the table; slumped in front of the television); a goat postman delivers a party invitation; the dog phones the cat, dresses in shirt and tie, chooses a present (thinking of a carrot, fruit, a football, a box), gives the rabbit a huge wrapped gift, joins the surprise party meal with cat, pig, rabbit and mouse, and ends dancing arm-in-arm with his friends. Feelings (grumpy→happy) and party-giving, told purely in pictures; the audio adds a getting-together song and party music.
- **Δ07 — The Selfish Giant (pp.152–154).** Six story cards adapting Wilde's tale: children playing in a lovely garden; the giant scaring them off; the giant alone inside his walled garden where it stays winter; children creeping back as spring follows them; the giant gently lifting a small boy into a blossoming tree; and the giant playing with the children in the restored garden. Sharing/kindness moral; seasons (winter vs spring) recycled as the story's engine; audio adds a sharing song.
- **Δ08 — The sailor and the mermaid (pp.157–159).** Two art cards — a painted portrait of a sailor and a Greek folk-art mermaid holding a ship among fish — introduce the tale; six sea flashcards (fish, starfish, shell, crab, seahorse, octopus); and two big colouring outlines, the sailor at his ship's wheel and the mermaid. Sea vocabulary and a sea tale; the audio adds a sailor action song.
- **Δ09 — Summer holidays: the lucky envelope (pp.160–165).** Four big holiday scenes — camping in the woods, a seaside pool deck with dolphins, a city street signed THEATRE, MUSEUM and GIFTSHOP, and a beach with surfing, swimming and a sandcastle — followed by four cut-out sheets that break the same scenes into pieces (tent, tree, ball and animals; pool, lounger, dolphin and drink; theatre/cinema, museum, gift shop, car and statue; beach ball, umbrella, sandcastle, flippers, ring and surfboards) to rebuild them. Holiday places and activities; the story and the "It's summer time" song are audio only.

*Alphabet strand in Cycle Δ:* J jungle (pp.133–134, a lion king and a small monkey), I Indian (pp.139–140, children in feather headdresses and a counting rhyme to four — the word is printed in its period form, capital-I "Indian"), D dog (pp.150–151, a big strong dog vs a small lazy one — size adjectives), G garden (pp.155–156, a goat eating grass in a garden — links back to the Giant's garden).

#### Cycle E — festivals and celebrations (PDF pp.166–194, closing track to p.195)

- **E01 — Halloween (pp.166–168).** A costume-party card (cowboy on a hobby horse, witch, wizard, skeleton, glowing pumpkin lantern), six flashcards (black cat, spider, witch, bat, pumpkin, skeleton) and a bat-wing outline to make a bat. Halloween vocabulary; audio "Bats are sleeping".
- **E02 — Christmas (pp.169–172).** A Santa's-workshop card (Santa and elves making and wrapping toys), six flashcards (star, stocking, angel, bell, bauble, present), a colour-by-number Christmas tree on a 1–10 grid with a colour key (red, blue, yellow, green, grey, brown, pink), and an outline copy of the workshop scene to colour. Christmas vocabulary; audio "The lights of the tree".
- **E03 — The Gingerbread Man (pp.175–179).** Nine story cards tell the tale in pictures only: the old woman takes him from the oven and he escapes through the window; the old couple chase him; he outruns a horse and passes a cow; he meets the fox, hesitates at the river, rides across on the fox's tail and then its nose, and is tossed and eaten. The worksheet is a blank gingerbread-man outline to decorate under the story's chase cry. A cumulative chase tale; the audio adds a counting song, "Five little cookies".
- **E04 — Carnival (pp.180–181).** Two photo cards — a street carnival parade and a collage of toddlers in fancy dress (lion, fox, owl, gnomes, ghost, sea-dragon, pirate, frog, Little Red Riding Hood, bee, Sesame-Street-style monsters, fairy) — plus four feelings-face flashcards reused from A04 (sad, happy, unwell/worried, surprised). Fancy-dress vocabulary; E04 has no audio track in the contents list.
- **E05 — Spring morning (pp.182–184).** Five paintings/drawings of spring (a figure in a flowering meadow, a bird among blossom, children cycling, a boy with a bicycle, an impressionist fishing scene) and two cut-out sheets of spring things — a boy on a bicycle, flowers, a butterfly, a girl picking flowers, a frog fishing, and a flower-decorated hat/plate craft. Spring through art and craft; song in audio.
- **E06 — The Easter Bunny (pp.185–189).** Seven story cards: the bunny with its basket of coloured eggs; children in a garden; the bunny hiding eggs by the tree and bushes; the egg hunt ("Look! An egg!"); and the children thanking the bunny ("Thank you! Happy Easter!"). Worksheets: number four mini-pictures into story order, and colour five patterned Easter eggs. Easter vocabulary and a thank-you exchange.
- **E07 — Mother's Day: mother's care (pp.192–194).** A photo card of mothers caring for small children in several countries (spoon-feeding, bottle-feeding, playing together, carrying, a doctor examining a baby held by its mother, a hug in a meadow), a flower-framed blank frame to make (for a photo or drawing), and a fold-and-make flowerpot card craft with printed folding diagrams. A celebration-of-mothers lesson; the making is the language work, with two songs in audio.
- **E08 — Make a circle (audio only).** The closing item exists only as the last audio track in the contents list (PDF p.195); there are no printed sheets for it.

*Alphabet strand in Cycle E:* X box (pp.173–174, a fox whose box holds a toy fox — has-got and what's-in questions in the rhyme), E egg (pp.190–191, an elephant who has an egg that two others want — placed late, inside the Easter lesson's run).

### Alphabet strand — complete list (one card + one tracing worksheet each)

Z zebra · C cat · L lion · N name · B bear · P pen · K kite · Y yo-yo · R rat · H hat · M monkey · T tiger · A apple · F fish · W water · U umbrella · O o'clock · V van · S socks · Q queen · J jungle · I Indian · D dog · G garden · X box · E egg. Every worksheet follows the same pattern: stroke-order diagrams for the capital and small letter, dotted letters and the key word to trace, the outline of the card picture to colour, and a 3–5 line rhyme built on the key word. The contents page (PDF p.195) also lists a separate song for every letter (Letters' Songs, tracks 30–55).

### Honest negatives — what this grade does NOT teach (yet)

- **No paginated reading text and almost no connected prose.** The only continuous written text in the whole pack is the Pinocchio gap-fill retelling (PDF p.144), the one-line captions on the rainbow cards, the short dialogue cards of Δ01–Δ02, and the letter rhymes. Everything else is single words, labels or nothing at all — the stories of Δ03, Δ06, Δ07, E03 and E06 are wordless picture sequences whose words exist only in the audio.
- **No grammar teaching as such.** There are no explanations, paradigms or drills. Structures appear only inside songs, rhymes and card captions: present continuous only for playground activities (Γ07), because-reasons only in Δ02, can/can't only through the B09 audio, possessive 's only inside two letter rhymes (S, and names in others). Past-tense forms occur inside the Pinocchio retelling but are never presented as a language point.
- **Time is o'clock only** — no half/quarter hours, no minutes (Γ02, and the O chant stops at 6.00).
- **Numbers stop at 20**, and even those are mostly sung/counted (1–10 as words on the caterpillar; 1–20 in B12's audio and counting sheet); no arithmetic, no ordinals except the decorative "1st" in "1st January" (PDF p.115).
- **Writing is tracing and copying only** — letters, single key words, day names, furniture words and a few short captions — plus three started lines on the A06 self-profile. No free sentence writing, no spelling rules, no punctuation teaching.
- **No phonics system** beyond one key word and a rhyme per letter; letter order is thematic, not alphabetical, and two letters (X, E) only arrive in the final cycle.
- **No instructions in Greek and almost none in English either** — no pupil-facing directions, exercises rubrics, word lists, glossary or answer material anywhere in the pack; it cannot be used without the teacher and the audio.
- **Holes in the printed pack itself:** B07 (Hokey Pokey) and E08 (Make a Circle) have audio but no printed sheets; B01, B04, Γ02, Γ06 and E04 have printed sheets but no audio track in the contents list; Δ04's two classical-music tracks have no printed material at all.
- **Dated content to flag, not hide:** the I-card teaches the word "Indian" for Native Americans, with children in feather headdresses (PDF pp.135, 139–140, and the Δ04 narrator figure), in the form in which it was printed in 2014.
## Grade 4 — Αγγλικά (Anglika), Student's Book, New Edition

### Identity block

- **Real title as printed (title page, PDF p. 4):** Αγγλικά Δ΄ Δημοτικού — Βιβλίο Μαθητή ("English, 4th Year of Primary School — Student's Book"). Authors named on the cover and title page: Αντιγόνη Μπρατσόλη (Antigoni Bratsoli, teacher) and Αγγελική Διαμαντίδου (Angeliki Diamantidou, former school adviser).
- **Publisher:** Ινστιτούτο Τεχνολογίας Υπολογιστών και Εκδόσεων «Διόφαντος» — ITYE "Diophantos" (Institute of Computer Technology and Publications), for the Υπουργείο Παιδείας, Θρησκευμάτων και Αθλητισμού (Ministry of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports) / Ινστιτούτο Εκπαιδευτικής Πολιτικής (Institute of Educational Policy). Original writing contract (ΑΝΑΔΟΧΟΣ ΣΥΓΓΡΑΦΗΣ) held by Ελληνικά Γράμματα, under the aegis of the Pedagogical Institute; illustrator Andreas Katsaounis.
- **Edition / year:** Revised edition — the cover carries the stamp «ΑΝΑΘΕΩΡΗΜΕΝΗ ΕΚΔΟΣΗ» ("Revised Edition", book code 10-0232), which is the basis for the record's "New Edition". No calendar year of publication is printed on the cover, title or imprint pages: the imprint (PDF p. 3) records the original edition under the Γ' Κ.Π.Σ. / ΕΠΕΑΕΚ ΙΙ programme and the reissue by ITYE Diophantos from a digital mock-up funded by ΕΣΠΑ / ΕΠ «Εκπαίδευση & Διά Βίου Μάθηση», Act «ΣΤΗΡΙΖΩ», with corrections approved by the board of the Institute of Educational Policy.
- **ISBN:** 978-960-06-2539-4 (printed on the back cover, PDF p. 1, with book code 0-10-0232 and barcode (01) 000000 0 10 0232 4).
- **Extent:** 170 PDF pages. The file is the full print sheet: PDF p. 1 is the front/back cover spread and PDF p. 170 repeats it; PDF p. 168 is blank and PDF p. 169 is the unnumbered statutory printing notice.
- **Page offset:** printed page = PDF page − 1 (printed = PDF − 1) throughout the numbered book. E.g. Contents are printed pp. 4–7 (PDF pp. 5–8), Unit 1 opens on printed p. 9 (PDF p. 10), and the Acknowledgements close on printed p. 166 (PDF p. 167). All page references below are to the **printed** pages.
- **Identity verdict:** The file matches the record exactly — Greece, Grade 4 (Δ΄ Δημοτικού), English, student's book, ITYE Diophantos / Ministry of Education (ebooks.edu.gr line). Through-line characters: Andrew Marinellis, a new pupil at the International School of Athens (half Greek, half British, from Oxford), his classmates Nick, Sophia and Betty, their teacher Mrs Stathaki, and Andrew's sister Amy.
- **How the book is built:** Ten units, each with Lesson 1 and Lesson 2 (story/dialogue, new words, songs and games) and a Lesson 3 cross-curricular project, followed by a bilingual self-assessment test; every unit opens with a "Strategy corner" self-check. Back matter: Appendix I "Work at your own pace" extra tasks (printed pp. 130–149), Appendix II "My Grammar Corner" (pp. 150–155), Appendix III Glossary — a fill-in Greek-meaning wordlist arranged by unit (pp. 156–160), Appendix IV Maps (pp. 161–165), Appendix V Acknowledgements (p. 166).

### Unit-by-unit summary

**Unit 1 — Back to School (pp. 9–20).** Andrew introduces his new school and class (Lesson 1, pp. 9–13): describing rooms and facilities of a school (classrooms, playground, basketball court, computer room, music room), counting pupils from a class survey table, and the numbers 20–99 as words (a counting song works in tens to ninety). Core structure: *there is / there are* with *is there…? / are there…?*, plus *have got* for possession. Lesson 2, "My timetable" (pp. 14–17), adds the days of the week and school subjects, reading Andrew's weekly timetable, comparing timetables (*have got / hasn't got* on a given day), and writing one's own timetable for a pen friend. Lesson 3 (pp. 18–20) is a poster project about the pupils' own school; self-assessment on pp. 19–20 tests *there is/are*, number arithmetic in words and the days of the week.

**Unit 2 — What's Your Favourite Hobby or Sport? (pp. 21–32).** Lesson 1, "My favourite sport" (pp. 21–25), is a playground dialogue in which Andrew prefers basketball to football; vocabulary for sports (football, volleyball, basketball, tennis, swimming, windsurfing, climbing, horse riding, cycling, sailing, plus cricket, rugby, hockey, baseball and tae kwon do matched to countries where they are popular). Language point: *I like / I don't like* + activity. Lesson 2, "Have you got a hobby?" (pp. 26–29), introduces third-person likes through Sophia's pen friend Olina from Thessaloniki: *he/she likes… / he/she doesn't like…*, hobby vocabulary (dancing, painting, reading, collecting things, singing, board games, taking photos, listening to music) and judging hobbies as interesting, boring, strange or fun. Lesson 3 (pp. 30–32) is an Olympic Games project — posters of Olympic sports and famous athletes, comparing Olympic sports past and present.

**Unit 3 — This Is Where I Live (pp. 33–44).** Lesson 1, "My country" (pp. 33–37): Andrew explains that the United Kingdom has four parts (England, Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland), with Oxford near the capital London; countries and nationalities (*I'm from Greece — I'm Greek*), *where are you from?*, capital cities worked from the maps in Appendix IV, and a flag-guessing game. Lesson 2, "My city" (pp. 38–41), contrasts Oxford and Athens and teaches city facilities (post office, theatre, museum, café, cinema, shopping centre, block of flats, sports centre, church, bank, supermarket, park, school) with *is there…? / are there…?* and the place phrases *next to*, *between* and *on the corner of*; a board game tours Greek sights (the White Tower, Vergina, Dodoni, Delphi, the Acropolis, Epidavros). Lesson 3 (pp. 42–44) is a project poster about a place in Greece.

**Unit 4 — Time (pp. 45–56).** Lesson 1, "Happy Birthday!" (pp. 45–49): a party invitation gives the occasion to teach the twelve months, the four seasons and telling the time — *it's … o'clock*, *half past*, *(a) quarter past / (a) quarter to* — practised against a Greek TV listings page. Lesson 2, "What's the weather like?" (pp. 50–53), sets a dialogue at Sophia's party where the weather turns; weather vocabulary (*hot, warm, chilly, cold, sunny, windy, cloudy, raining, snowing*), a weather song, and present simple for what people do in particular months and seasons (*in* + month/season, *on* + day). Lesson 3 (pp. 54–56) projects on weather and climate around the world — houses, food and jobs in different climates — and a poem about a favourite season.

**Unit 5 — Habits and Customs (pp. 57–68).** Lesson 1, "It's only a dream!" (pp. 57–61): Betty dreams of living in Peter Pan's Neverland, which sets up the present simple for daily routines with the adverbs of frequency *always, usually, often, sometimes, never* and routine phrases (brush my teeth, do my homework, make my bed, get up early, clean up my room, take a bath/exercise, wash my hands). Lesson 2, "British customs" (pp. 62–65), describes Christmas and Halloween in Britain in the present simple (decorating the tree, stockings and presents opened on Christmas Day, carols, roast turkey and Christmas pudding; pumpkins, Jack-o'-lanterns and trick-or-treat costumes on 31 October), adds a listening on Bonfire Night (5 November), and asks pupils to write about Christmas in Greece. Lesson 3 (pp. 66–68) projects on habit surveys and on Christmas/Easter customs in Greece and other countries.

**Unit 6 — Animals (pp. 69–80).** Lesson 1, "My pet" (pp. 69–73), is built around a child's poem about a dog, Archie; pet and farm animals (goldfish, dog, cat, bird, iguana, sheep, cow, duck, tortoise) matched to what they do, animal sounds in a pet-shop song, and writing a riddle about a favourite animal (where it lives, what it looks like — *has got* for description — what it eats and does). Lesson 2 (pp. 74–77) is a factual visit to the Sea Turtle Rescue Centre: the loggerhead turtle *caretta caretta* presented in present-simple fact statements (habitat, size, eggs, survival), a parallel listening on the monk seal *Monachus monachus*, and a guessing game using a fact table for the giant panda, Sumatran tiger, brown bear and wolf, with *does it…? — yes, it does / no, it doesn't*. Lesson 3 (pp. 78–80) is an endangered-animals project and leaflet, pointing to Archelon, Arcturos, MOm, Medasset and WWF Hellas.

**Unit 7 — What Are You Doing? (pp. 81–92).** Lesson 1, "Helping around the house" (pp. 81–85), introduces the present continuous for actions happening now, through a kitchen dialogue and household chores (making the beds, setting the table, sweeping, washing up, washing the floor, ironing, watering the plants, cooking), with question and short-answer forms (*what are you doing? — I am…; is he…? — yes, he is / no, he isn't*) and a miming game. Lesson 2, "What do you do?" (pp. 86–89), contrasts jobs as facts with actions in progress — present simple vs. present continuous: parents' jobs (teacher, doctor, hairdresser, bus driver, waiter, reporter, baker, policeman, shop assistant, nurse, firefighter), where each works and what each is doing in a picture. Lesson 3 (pp. 90–92) projects on interviewing a local professional and researching an old or disappearing job (the self-assessment uses the roving/street photographer).

**Unit 8 — Around the City (pp. 93–104).** Lesson 1, "At the park" (pp. 93–97): a school outing teaches rules through signs — the imperative (*keep off the grass; don't litter / don't pick the flowers / don't play football*) and *can / can't* for permission — extended to writing school rules, the Hokey Cokey song and "Simon says". Lesson 2 (pp. 98–101) brings a traffic warden, Mr Kanellopoulos, into class: road signs and road-safety vocabulary (crossing, traffic lights, seat belt, pavement, pedestrian), adding *must / mustn't* for obligation, and a blindfold treasure-hunt game practising *turn left / turn right / go straight ahead*. Lesson 3 (pp. 102–104) projects on making large road signs and writing road-safety advice for pedestrians.

**Unit 9 — The School Party (pp. 105–116).** Lesson 1, "At the supermarket" (pp. 105–109), plans an end-of-year party shopping trip: food vocabulary and, as the unit's grammar core, countable vs. uncountable nouns — *a/an* and *some*, *how many…?* vs. *how much…?* — plus a budgeting task with euro prices and weights, and a listening on healthy eating. Lesson 2, "Let's make some sandwiches" (pp. 110–113), turns quantity language to cooking: recipe verbs (*slice, boil, spread, add, mix, grate, drain, beat, peel, pour*) used as imperatives, sequencing a potato-salad recipe, completing a Spanish omelette recipe, and *much / many* in context ("don't put much butter"). Lesson 3 (pp. 114–116) is a "Recipes from around the world" project.

**Unit 10 — Enjoy Your Holidays! (pp. 117–129).** A closing review unit. Lesson 1, "Our yearbook" (pp. 117–121), has the four main characters write yearbook entries about themselves and their families, recycling the whole book — *I've got / haven't got, I can / can't, I like / don't like*, habits, pets, sports, food and family — through a "find someone who…" survey, personal-information writing and a 20-question "Can you remember?" game that quizzes facts from Units 1–9. Lesson 2 (pp. 122–124, ending printed on p. 129) is a present-simple story, "Dairy the fairy", whose cat Milky keeps eating her milk and cheese and is magically transformed; pupils guess the ending before reading it. Lesson 3 (pp. 125–129) is the class-yearbook project — interviewing a classmate with Wh-questions — plus the final self-assessment (forming Wh-questions with *what, where, how often, how many, how much*) and the book-wide "secret word contest" score page (p. 126).

**Appendices (pp. 130–166).** Appendix I repeats and extends one task per lesson at the pupil's own pace, with instructions largely in Greek, including extra readings (an Oxford Covered Market text, p. 135; a dolphin fact file, p. 140; the disappearing ice-cream seller, p. 141; a Romanian folk tale about a mother rabbit outwitting a wolf, pp. 148–149). Appendix II, "My Grammar Corner" (pp. 150–155, explanations in Greek), tabulates exactly the structures taught: *there is/are* (1.1), *have got* (1.2), *I like / he likes* (2.1–2.2), asking where someone is from (3.1), telling the time and *in/on* time phrases (4.1–4.2), present simple with third-person *-s* spelling rules and adverbs of frequency (5.1), *do/does* questions (6.2), present continuous with *-ing* spelling rules and the present simple vs. present continuous contrast (7.1–7.2), the imperative (8.1a), *can/can't* for permission (8.1b), *must/mustn't* for obligation (8.2) and countable/uncountable nouns with *some, a/an, how many / how much* (9.1). Appendix III is a fill-in glossary by unit and theme; Appendix IV prints the UK, Europe and world maps used from Unit 3 on; Appendix V credits the conservation organisations and photographers whose material is reproduced.

*Reading note:* a few running heads are misprinted in the book itself — e.g. printed p. 113 is headed "Lesson 1 Happy Birthday!" although it is the Unit 9 Lesson 2 game page, and printed pp. 123 and 125 carry wrong lesson heads over the "Dairy the fairy" continuation and the Unit 10 Lesson 3 project. The lesson content itself is in the correct order.

### Citation check

### Honest negatives — major structures not yet taught

Judged from the unit contents (printed pp. 4–7) and the Grammar Corner's own index (pp. 150–155), which between them list every structure the book claims to teach:

- **No past tenses.** There is no past simple (or any past narration) anywhere: even the one full story, "Dairy the fairy" (pp. 122–124, 129), is narrated entirely in the present simple, and no irregular past forms are introduced.
- **No future forms.** *Will* and future *going to* are not taught; "going to" occurs only incidentally, untaught, in a teacher's introduction on p. 98.
- **No present perfect, no conditionals, no passive voice, and no reported speech.**
- **No comparison of adjectives.** Comparatives and superlatives are never presented as a structure (no *-er / more… than* lesson in any unit or in the Grammar Corner).
- **No systematic possessives or pronouns work.** Possessive *'s* and possessive adjectives appear inside texts (Andrew's timetable, my father's job) but are never tabulated or taught as a point; likewise articles are limited to *a/an* with countable nouns in Unit 9 — there is no teaching of *the* vs. *a/an*.
- **Modality is narrow:** only *can/can't* for permission (and incidentally for ability in Unit 10 review) and *must/mustn't* for obligation; no *should, have to, may* or *would*.
- **Question forms stay basic:** yes/no questions and the Wh-words met in context, gathered only in the final self-assessment (p. 127); there are no question tags, no negative questions, and time reference never goes beyond clock time, days, months and seasons.
## Grade 5 — Αγγλικά (Anglika), Pupil's Book, Revised Edition — as printed: «ΑΓΓΛΙΚΑ / English 5th Grade, Ε΄ Δημοτικού, Pupil's Book»

### Identity block

- **Identity verdict:** The file is what the record says — the Greek Ministry Grade 5 English pupil's book. The cover (PDF p. 1, a combined front-cover / spine / back-cover press sheet) reads «ΑΓΓΛΙΚΑ — English 5th Grade», «Ε΄ Δημοτικού» and "Pupil's Book", under the Ministry of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports and the Institute of Educational Policy. The title page (PDF p. 4) repeats "English 5th Grade — Pupil's Book".
- **Record-title note:** The record's "Vivlio Mathiti" (Βιβλίο Μαθητή) is the generic Greek for "student's book"; the book itself uses the English "Pupil's Book". The record's "New Edition" corresponds to the round stamp printed on the cover, «ΑΝΑΘΕΩΡΗΜΕΝΗ ΕΚΔΟΣΗ» — literally **Revised Edition**, book code 10-0233.
- **Authors:** Eleftheria-Klio Kolovou (Ελευθερία-Κλειώ Κολοβού) and Anna Kraniotou (Άννα Κρανιώτου), both listed on the cover and, in the imprint (PDF p. 5), as PE6 teachers. Illustration by Elisavet Vavouri; original-edition contractor S. Patakis A.E.E.E.; writing done under the Pedagogical Institute.
- **Publisher:** Institute of Computer Technology and Publications «Diophantos» (ΙΤΥΕ «ΔΙΟΦΑΝΤΟΣ»), for the Ministry of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports / Institute of Educational Policy (ebooks.edu.gr series). The imprint (PDF p. 5) says the reissue was produced by ITYE Diophantos from a digital layout funded under ESPA / "STIRIZO", with corrections approved by the Institute of Educational Policy board.
- **ISBN:** 978-960-06-2567-7 (printed on the back cover, PDF p. 1). Book code: 0-10-0233.
- **Edition / year:** No single publication year is printed on the imprint page. The Revised Edition is the 10-0233 issue; internal production stamps in this PDF run from 2014–2016 for most signatures, with some gatherings re-dated 2020, 2022 and 2024, and the closing legal notice dated 05/10/2023 — i.e. this PDF is a later digital assembly of the revised edition, not a new textbook.
- **Extent:** 170 PDF pages. PDF pp. 1 and 170 are the same cover press sheet (front + spine + back in one spread); PDF pp. 2–3 are blank; printed content runs to printed p. 168 (the Greek legal/copyright notice).
- **Page offset:** **Printed page = PDF page − 1** throughout the body (e.g. PDF p. 15 = printed p. 14; PDF p. 164 = printed p. 163). All page references below are printed pages, with PDF pages in brackets where the citation check needs them.
- **Cast and design (introduction, printed p. 7):** Three continuing characters carry the book — Kostas from Greece, Nadine from France and Mark from England — who chat online through the year and finally meet on holiday. The book has 10 units of 3 lessons each, a Self Assessment Test at the end of every unit, and appendices with extra activities, a "Discover Grammar" section, an irregular-verb list and maps. A companion Workbook exists but is not in this file.

### Unit-by-unit summary (own words)

**Unit 1 — Internet Friends Around Europe (printed pp. 13–24)**
- *Lesson 1, "Do You Like Computers?" (pp. 13–17):* A computer-shop picture introduces the parts of a computer and their prices (screen, mouse, scanner, printer, keyboard, tower, speakers, headphones). Pupils discuss what computers are good and bad for, read a short e-mail from Connor in Ireland about how he uses e-mail and the Internet, and survey free-time activities. **First arrival — likes, dislikes and preferences (p. 17):** *like / don't like / enjoy / hate* + *-ing* or noun, and *prefer X to Y*.
- *Lesson 2, "Internet Friends" (pp. 18–21):* The three main characters meet in an online chat and introduce themselves — ages, schools, likes. Country-and-nationality words and flags follow (with "good morning" in several languages in the appendix). **First arrival — the Present Simple as a taught system (p. 20):** affirmative, negative and question forms for talking about school life and routines, with the third-person *-s/-es/-ies* spelling changes.
- *Lesson 3, "The United Kingdom" (pp. 22–24):* A leaflet-style text on the British Isles, the UK and Ireland — capitals, populations, national flowers — mined for information into a table; the project is a matching leaflet about Greece. Self Assessment Test (pp. 23–24 in the printed footer sequence).

**Unit 2 — School Life and the World Around Us (printed pp. 25–36)**
- *Lesson 1, School life and feelings (pp. 26–29):* A page from Mark's school newspaper (an e-mail about a Eurodisney trip, a canteen menu, a Halloween party invitation) teaches text types and feeling words (excited, sad, bored, angry, sorry, happy). Pupils role-play buying snacks, learning British pounds and pence against euros. **First arrival — time prepositions *at / on / in* (p. 28).** (Note: the lesson's printed heading repeats Unit 1's "Do You Like Computers?" — see Honest negatives.)
- *Lesson 2, "Talking About Habits — Good & Bad" (pp. 30–33):* A radio interview with a famous sports person is completed from listening, sorted into good and bad habits, and reused as a model for interviewing a famous visitor. **First arrival — adverbs of frequency (p. 32):** *always–usually–often–sometimes–rarely/seldom–never* with rough percentage values and their position in the sentence; a class questionnaire and pie-chart survey of pupils' own habits follows.
- *Lesson 3, "Customs Around the World" (pp. 34–36):* Short notes on customs in Japan, Britain and the USA, the appendix's "DOs and DON'Ts in England", and a cross-curricular project comparing Greek manners and customs with other countries'. Self Assessment Test (pp. 35–36).

**Unit 3 — Places (printed pp. 37–48)**
- *Lesson 1, "The Place We Live In" (pp. 38–41):* The three friends describe where they live (London, Athens–Nea Ionia, Marseilles), their parents' jobs and how they travel to work. **First arrival — expressing opinions and making suggestions (p. 40):** *I think that…, I don't think…, It seems to me…, In my opinion…*, plus *Why don't you…?, How about…?, Let's…*. A WWF-style leaflet prompts pupils' own suggestions for city problems.
- *Lesson 2, "How Can I Get To…?" (pp. 42–44):* Directions on real maps — Nea Ionia (Kostas's house to the Youth Centre) and the Acropolis area — with a "Simon Says" movement game. **First arrival — direction language (p. 44):** *go straight ahead, turn left/right into…, take the first/second turning, on your right/left, at the end of the street*. Pupils write a note giving a visitor directions.
- *Lesson 3, "Talking About a City in Greece" (pp. 45–48):* A guidebook text about a north-western Greek lakeside town (Ioannina, unnamed in the task) is analysed for how a place description is organised — location, surroundings, old and new town — as a model for a group project on another city. Self Assessment Test (pp. 47–48).

**Unit 4 — Christmas Everywhere (printed pp. 49–60)**
- *Lesson 1, "Getting Ready for Christmas" (pp. 50–53):* Making decorations in France (glue, scissors, card, string), then a reading about dolphin therapy giving children with special needs a Christmas day out in Florida. **First arrival — Present Continuous contrasted with Present Simple (p. 52):** what people *usually do* versus what they *are doing this year / today*. Writing task: a holiday postcard.
- *Lesson 2, "Kostas Is in New York for Christmas" (pp. 54–57):* Pancake-making in the cousins' kitchen (sequencing a recipe), **sense verbs (p. 55)** — *look / taste / smell / feel* + adjective — for food and presents, Christmas customs matched to five countries, and a full kourabiedes/koulouria recipe to follow.
- *Lesson 3, "A Christmas Song" (pp. 58–60):* The class sings "Santa Claus Is Coming to Town", memorises a Christmas poem from the appendix, and chooses between projects on Christmas traditions worldwide or on children who cannot celebrate. Self Assessment Test (pp. 59–60).

**Unit 5 — Ready for Action (environment) (printed pp. 61–72)**
- *Lesson 1, "An Ambitious Class Project" (pp. 62–64):* Kostas's class plans a recycling campaign. **First arrival — the future, taught as one system (p. 63):** *be going to* for plans and intentions, the Present Continuous for fixed arrangements, and *will* for predictions and hypotheses, including *If my plan works out, we'll…*. A "What a Waste!" quiz makes pupils calculate the wood, water and energy cost of landfilled paper.
- *Lesson 2, "Let's Do It!!!" (pp. 65–69):* A scored "Do you love our planet?" questionnaire, campaign planning, shopping tips for reducing waste, and **first arrival — modals *can / must / should* as a taught set (p. 68):** ability, obligation and advice for protecting the environment. A WWF text on Mediterranean forest fires closes the lesson.
- *Lesson 3, "My Work Can Make a Difference!" (pp. 70–72):* Mediation work — turning Greek WWF visitor guidelines for Zagorochoria into English advice lists — and a group project writing to the mayor (recycling bins, battery bins, a planting expedition). Self Assessment Test (pp. 71–72).

**Unit 6 — Good, Better, Best! (printed pp. 73–84)**
- *Lesson 1, "Choosing a Present" (pp. 74–77):* Comparing shop items, prices and holiday places (Brighton vs Blackpool), and a city-versus-countryside chat. **First arrival — comparatives (p. 75 focus box):** regular *-er than / more … than* forms, used to write a report comparing two towns from a data table (Athens vs London).
- *Lesson 2, "World Records" (pp. 78–81):* Guinness-style records (tallest woman, largest palace, a plane pulled by hand, a car balanced on a head, the longest venomous snake) and a laptop-buying comparison. **First arrival — superlatives (p. 80):** *the -est / the most …*, including the irregular *good–better–best* and *bad–worse–worst* sets. Pupils write an advertisement using superlatives.
- *Lesson 3, "A Knowledge Quiz" (pp. 82–84):* A world-knowledge quiz built entirely on comparative/superlative questions (highest mountain, smallest country, fastest animal), then groups write and play their own quiz. Self Assessment Test (pp. 83–84).

**Unit 7 — Going Back in Time (printed pp. 85–96)**
- *Lesson 1, "Famous People of the Past" (pp. 86–89):* Shakespeare (born 1564, 37 plays, the Globe) and a comparison chart of the Globe and Epidaurus theatres. **First arrival — Past Simple, affirmative (p. 88):** taught through a short biography of El Greco, with the regular spelling rules (add *-ed*, *-d* after *e*, *-ied* after consonant + *y*, doubling after a stressed short vowel).
- *Lesson 2, "Past Experiences" (pp. 90–93):* A detective story — a police interrogation about a bank-robbery alibi, the girlfriend's conflicting version, and a second witness — gives natural work on sequencing past events. **First arrival — Past Simple negatives and questions (p. 92):** *did / didn't*, short answers, and *was/were* questions, modelled on a mini-biography of the painter Theophanis.
- *Lesson 3, "Alexander the Great" (pp. 94–96):* A text on Alexander's tactics (Issus, the siege of Tyre, settling troops in conquered lands) read critically — pupils must argue from evidence why he was "great". Self Assessment Test (pp. 95–96), including a ghost-dialogue with Anne Boleyn.

**Unit 8 — All About Stories (printed pp. 97–108)**
- *Lesson 1, "Fairy Tales" (pp. 98–101):* A jumbled-print opening of a fairy tale (a prince searching for a real princess; a stormy night and a knock at the castle door) is reconstructed, listened to in full, cast, dramatised, and extended into a puppet / Karagiozis shadow-theatre play. **First arrival — Past Continuous (p. 100):** *was/were + -ing* for past actions in progress, framed by the storm scene.
- *Lesson 2, "What an Experience!" (pp. 102–105):* An online chat retelling a frightening practical joke, a listening about a family questioned after a gunshot nearby, and **first arrival — Past Simple and Past Continuous together (p. 104):** interrupted actions with *while / when*. Pupils write their own short story with linking words (*first, then, after that, finally, as soon as, while, when*).
- *Lesson 3, "A Traditional Story" (pp. 106–108):* Easter customs as story material — an extract (in translation) from Papadiamantis on a village Easter, plus Easter in Norway, with Mexico and Africa covered in the appendix. Self Assessment Test (pp. 107–108) drills the two past tenses and retells the Golden Fish tale.

**Unit 9 — Amazing People and Places (printed pp. 109–120)**
- *Lesson 1, "She Has Helped Save Gorillas" (pp. 110–113):* Dian Fossey and the poaching of baby gorillas, then **first arrival — the Present Perfect (p. 111):** presented as the tense that connects past and present — for news, with *ever / recently / yet / never*, and for situations continuing "up to now". Listening on Mikis Theodorakis after a clip of *Zorba the Greek*; pupils list their own lifetime achievements so far.
- *Lesson 2, "A Trip to Dubai!" (pp. 114–117):* A dialogue about a Dubai trip (including its artificial snow centre) and an Irish children's art competition article. **First arrival — Past Simple vs Present Perfect contrasted (p. 115):** "finished actions" at a definite time against "any time up to now", drawn on a timeline. Writing: a letter swapping travel experiences.
- *Lesson 3, "Newspapers & Headlines" (pp. 118–120):* How headlines compress the Present Simple, how broadcast news uses the Present Perfect, and *just* for fresh announcements; the class then plans its own school newspaper (guide in the appendix). Self Assessment Test (pp. 119–120) practises *just / already / yet* and choosing between the two tenses.

**Unit 10 — Summer Is Here! (printed pp. 121–132)**
- *Lesson 1, "At the Airport" (pp. 122–125):* Tourist-arrival figures for Greece, Nadine's arrival at Athens airport, flight-announcement boards (a mediation task explaining a Greek board to a Canadian visitor), and **a full tense revision (p. 124)** — Present Simple, Present Perfect, Past Simple and future set side by side on one timeline of a traveller's day. Project: present Athens International Airport from a data table.
- *Lesson 2, "Tourists Love Visiting Places" (pp. 126–129):* A parliamentary motion text calling for the return of the Parthenon Marbles, a class debate for and against, **position language for describing a picture** (*in the top left-hand corner, in the middle, at the bottom…*, p. 127) with a Chagall painting listening, and restaurant menus weighed against the food pyramid.
- *Lesson 3, "Myths and Legends" (pp. 130–132):* A diary-writing task filling in Nadine's Athens visit day by day, the Robin Hood text in the appendix (how he got his name and who the Merry Men were), and a portfolio project on gods of other civilisations (Aztecs, Incas, Vikings). Self Assessment Test (pp. 131–132) is a final mixed-tense check.

**Appendices (printed pp. 133–168)**
- *"It's Your Choice!" differentiated activities (pp. 133–152):* extra listening/reading per unit — "good morning" in ten languages, symbols of Great Britain, fish and chips and DOs and DON'Ts in England, London and Frankfurt/Venice map work, a Christmas poem, environmental project planners and a recycling board game, advert-writing (AIDA), Shakespeare fact file, Easter in Norway/Mexico/Africa with "Happy Easter" in many languages, how to create a school newspaper, Heathrow data, both sides of the Parthenon Marbles debate written by New York schoolchildren, an Athens sightseeing itinerary, and the Robin Hood extract.
- *"Discover Grammar" (pp. 153–161):* the book's grammar in reference form, unit by unit — likes/preferences and Present Simple (U1); time prepositions and frequency adverbs (U2); opinion and suggestion formulas (U3); Present Simple vs Continuous and sense verbs (U4); the three future forms with the full *will* paradigm (U5, pp. 155–156); modals *can/must/should* (U5); comparative and superlative formation, regular and irregular (U6); Past Simple with spelling rules and time expressions (U7); Past Continuous (U8); Present Perfect (U9).
- *Irregular verbs list (p. 162):* present / past / past participle in two alphabetical runs (be–fly and have–write in the extraction order).
- *Maps (pp. 163–167):* Athens Metro map, London Tube map and further map plates (image-only pages).
- *Legal notice (p. 168, in Greek):* state textbooks printed by ITYE–Diophantos are distributed free to public schools; reproduction without written permission of the Ministry / ITYE–Diophantos is prohibited.
