### Honest negatives

- **No publication year is printed** on the cover, title page or imprint pages; only the reissue note and in-file production stamps (2015–2024, varying by section) are present. Any catalogue year for this book comes from outside the book itself.
- **The workbook has no listening component:** unlike the Student's Book, it sets no audio tasks (its only CD reference is inside a classroom-instructions matching exercise, printed p. 3). Nothing in it needs to be verified against audio.
- **The workbook has no self-assessment pages and no answer key** for its main tasks; the only printed answers found are the emoticon matching key on printed p. 115 (and its appendix repeat). The "It's up to you!" appendix is a scaffolded re-do, not a key.
- **The Sources heading appears to carry a misprint:** printed p. 167 heads the list "ΠΗΓΕΣ ΚΕΙΜΕΝΩΝ & ΕΙΚΟΝΩΝ ΠΟΥ ΧΡΗΣΙΜΟΠΟΙΗΘΗΚΑΝ ΓΙΑ: Αγγλικά Α΄ Γυμνασίου – Επίπεδο Προχωρημένων – **Βιβλίο Μαθητή**" (Student's Book), although the items listed are this workbook's texts. Reported as printed; the list itself is the workbook's.
- **Unit-title mismatch with the Student's Book:** Unit 6 is headed "Volunteers wanted!" in the workbook's contents and opener, against "Teens in Action" in the Student's Book; lesson titles inside the unit agree.
- **A few pages are blank or near-blank in the text layer** (PDF p. 5; printed p. 130, the appendix divider, which carries only its page number; printed p. 168, blank between the two sources pages); picture-only tasks (word searches, crosswords, photo labelling) are described from the rendered pages and task instructions, not from extracted text.
- Dated content is part of the book as printed: the news reports are from 2002–2006, the TV guide is a January listings page of that era, house and zoo prices are in euros of the period, and several web sources cited in the texts (e.g. santaclausschool.com, oldsuperstitions.com) are period addresses, not verified as live.
## Grade 7 (Beginners) — Αγγλικά, Student's Book — *Think Teen! 1st Grade of Junior High School, Student's Book (Αρχάριοι)*

### Identity block

- **Real title as printed:** *Think Teen!* — "1st Grade of Junior High School / STUDENT'S BOOK", with the stream word **Αρχάριοι** (Beginners) printed in white script on the front cover, in red on the title page, and on the imprint title page. The sources appendix (printed p. 199) names the book in Greek as "Αγγλικά Α΄ Γυμνασίου – Επίπεδο Αρχαρίων – Βιβλίο Μαθητή" (English, 1st Grade of Gymnasio – Beginners Level – Student's Book). Α΄ Γυμνασίου is the first year of Greek junior high school, i.e. Grade 7.
- **Stream verdict:** BEGINNERS — confirmed. This is the **αρχαρίων** book, not the Advanced (Προχωρημένοι) book. The word Αρχάριοι appears on the front cover, the spine, the title page (PDF p. 2) and the imprint title page (PDF p. 4), and the cover stamp reads "ΑΝΑΘΕΩΡΗΜΕΝΗ ΕΚΔΟΣΗ 21-0204" (Revised Edition).
- **Authors:** Ευαγγελία Καραγιάννη (Evangelia Karagianni), Βασιλική Κουή (Vasiliki Koui), Αικατερίνη Νικολάκη (Aikaterini Nikolaki) — the same author team as the Advanced volume. Writing contractor named on the imprint page: Ελληνικά Γράμματα (Ellinika Grammata), under the auspices of the Pedagogical Institute.
- **Publisher:** Ινστιτούτο Τεχνολογίας Υπολογιστών και Εκδόσεων «ΔΙΟΦΑΝΤΟΣ» (Institute of Computer Technology and Publications "Diophantos" — ITYE Diophantos), for the Υπουργείο Παιδείας, Θρησκευμάτων και Αθλητισμού (Ministry of Education, Religions and Sports) / Ινστιτούτο Εκπαιδευτικής Πολιτικής (Institute of Educational Policy). Distributed via ebooks.edu.gr.
- **ISBN:** 978-960-06-2681-0 (printed on the back cover). **Book code:** 0-21-0204 (cover barcode element: (01) 000000 0 21 0204 7). The Advanced parallel volume is code 0-21-0205 / ISBN 978-960-06-2684-1, so the two streams are numbered as a pair.
- **Edition / year:** No calendar year is printed on the cover, title page or imprint pages. The book is marked as a revised edition; the imprint page states the reissue was produced by ITYE Diophantos from a digital mockup funded under ESPA / "ΣΤΗΡΙΖΩ", with corrections approved by the Institute of Educational Policy. In-file production stamps are dated 10/2/2015 and 20/1/2016, and the cover file stamp is dated 20/10/2023. (No publication year is asserted beyond what is printed/stamped.)
- **Extent:** 214 PDF pages; 204 printed pages plus unnumbered front matter and cover spreads.
- **Page offset:** **printed page = PDF page − 9** throughout the numbered body and appendices (e.g. printed p. 1 = PDF p. 10; printed p. 131 = PDF p. 140; printed p. 204 = PDF p. 213). PDF pp. 1 and 214 are the cover spread; PDF pp. 2–4 are the title and imprint pages; PDF p. 5 is blank; PDF pp. 6–9 are the Contents; printed p. 198 (PDF p. 207) and printed p. 203 (PDF p. 212) are blank.
- **Cast / frame:** A recurring group of teenage "e-friends" linked by the THINK TEEN e-programme, introduced by David from England (printed p. 2): Magda in Nafplio and Helen in Plaka, Athens (Greece), Jennifer/Jenny in Cambridge, Michael in Liverpool, Pablo in Lisbon, Antonio in Florence, Jean Paul in Tours, Silou from Indonesia, Daphne from Patmos, and key pals further away such as Nicole in the Australian outback. Units are anchored in their classrooms, e-mails and e-projects rather than in a camp.

### What "Beginners" means here — and what the book assumes

Despite the Αρχάριοι (Beginners) label, this is **not an absolute-zero, ab initio book**, and it does not teach the alphabet or letter sounds. It is the lower stream of a streamed Grade 7 class in a system where pupils have already had English in primary school, and it treats that primary English as something to revise and build on, at revision speed:

- Unit 1 (only six pages) already expects learners to spell their names letter by letter in English, answer Wh-questions about name, surname and country, and work with *be*, *there is / there are*, colours, numbers 1–10 and classroom objects — all presented as familiar material to organise, not as first encounters.
- The first reading text (printed p. 2) is a full paragraph in the first person that already uses a contracted *have got* form, and by printed p. 9 learners read four self-introduction paragraphs of roughly 60–80 words each. By printed p. 14 they are mining a genuine children's-novel extract — written in the Past Simple, a tense this book does not teach until Unit 7 — for adjectives only.
- There is no alphabet, phonics or handwriting strand. Pronunciation appears only as short embedded links (a tongue twister on p. 15, sentence stress on p. 52, dictionary stress marks on p. 68, question intonation on p. 95).
- The grammar ceiling is correspondingly lower than the Advanced volume's: the course ends with the Past Simple and the three future forms. There is **no Present Perfect, no Passive, no Past Continuous contrast, no relative clauses, no gerunds and no *used to*** — all of which the Advanced Grade 7 book does teach. Shared lesson and unit titles (e.g. "Travel Plans!", "In the year 2525!", "TEEN best-sellers!") are reworked at this lower level, in a different unit order.

### Unit-by-unit summary (own words; printed page references)

**Unit 1 — Welcome! (printed pp. 1–6).** A single short opening unit, not split into lessons. Learners guess which language photographed teenagers are greeting each other in, then meet David, who introduces the THINK TEEN e-programme and its worldwide key pals. Learners complete personal-detail cards for themselves and a partner (name, surname, country, spelling), read English words on public signs, pick English loanwords out of short Greek dialogues by ear, and work through colours (including colour idioms, with Greek equivalents), classroom language (asking for a meaning, repetition, help, permission to go out) and numbers/classroom objects with *there is / there are*. A class survey covers favourite number, animal, hobby and type of music. Projects: a collage of foreign-language signs found locally, and a noticeboard list of English words used in Greek, with a short exercise tracing Greek loanwords to their source languages.

**Unit 2 — All About Us (printed pp. 7–24).** Three lessons. *Lesson 1, "Hello, there!" (p. 8):* a jigsaw reading of four e-friend profiles (Magda, Pablo, Jennifer, Antonio) covering country, hometown, family, school subjects, likes and abilities; sports-and-activities vocabulary from two sports-centre leaflets; a geography quiz and guessing game on countries, capitals and languages; the verb *be* presented in the Grammar Link; writing is a drafted-and-redrafted "This is me!" profile for the e-notice board. *Lesson 2, "A collection of thimbles!" (p. 13):* favourite possessions and collections heard in a Cambridge classroom; adjectives sorted by opinion, size, age, colour and material, practised on an adapted extract from Lemony Snicket's *A Series of Unfortunate Events — The Bad Beginning* (credited on the page as the 2005 HarperCollins edition); *have got* in the Grammar Link; a memory game on things in a school bag; writing about a favourite possession. *Lesson 3, "Feel at home!" (p. 18):* Helen's e-mail describing her Plaka neighbourhood under the Acropolis to an exchange visitor; places-and-buildings vocabulary from signs and notices; plural nouns; *there is / there are* with *some / any*; prepositions of place in a spot-the-difference street task. Projects: presenting your own neighbourhood, and a favourite-possessions poster. Self-assessment pp. 23–24, with a focus on speaking strategies.

**Unit 3 — Day in Day Out (printed pp. 25–40).** Three lessons; the Present Simple unit. *Lesson 1, "My Day!" (p. 26):* Jean Paul from Tours writes a "My school day" e-project entry describing his routine in detail — getting up at 7, walking/cycling to school, a long lunch break at home, guitar, homework, tennis, bed around 11 — supported by daily-routine and sports vocabulary (*go / play / do* + sports), telling the time, and adverbs of frequency. *Lesson 2, "Greetings from Australia!" (p. 31):* an Australia quiz (key on p. 131), then Jennifer's school-newspaper article about her key pal Nicole, who lives in the Central Australian outback and studies through a "school of the air" — short on-air lessons with a teacher seen on a computer screen, work sent by e-mail, five to six hours of study a day; a Sydney pupil's timetable is compared with the learners' own, and school subjects are named and liked/disliked. *Lesson 3, "This is my job!" (p. 35):* an interview with Jerry Young, the chef at Jennifer's Cambridge school, about his hours, cooking and enjoyment of the job; jobs vocabulary (what a vet, architect, secretary, pilot and others do) and "work" idioms; Wh-questions in the Grammar Link; learners role-play reporter interviews about jobs. Project: professions. Self-assessment pp. 39–40, with a focus on reading strategies.

**Unit 4 — Ecofriendly (printed pp. 41–56).** Three lessons. *Lesson 1, "Let's go to the zoo!" (p. 42):* David's class visit to London Zoo — map symbols, and a guidebook page (credited as adapted from the London Zoo 2001 guide) on the recommended route, information kiosk, lost property, first aid and meeting places; the imperative and *if* + present sentences for instructions and advice in the Grammar Link. *Lesson 2, "In the wild!" (p. 46):* a carnivore/herbivore/omnivore quiz, then David's project on animals in danger — encyclopaedia-style entries on the timber wolf, the brown bear and the rhino giving height, weight, diet, pack/family life and hibernation, each with personal yes/no prompts; *can / can't* for ability; project: animal-facts posters. *Lesson 3, "Let's go green!" (p. 50):* a recycling poster sent between e-friends (sorting rubbish, buying recyclable products, forming a school eco team), environment verb collocations (cut down/plant trees, waste/save water, kill/protect animals), a radio programme about protecting animals, and *must / mustn't* for obligation and prohibition; writing is an e-mail about protecting the environment. Self-assessment pp. 55–56.

**Unit 5 — Teens in Action! (printed pp. 57–72).** Three lessons; the Present Continuous unit (the title is shared with a different unit in the Advanced book, but the content is not). *Lesson 1, "It's on the notice board!" (p. 58):* Michael's Liverpool school noticeboard (basketball tickets, a band seeking a keyboard player, a drawing competition, a healthy-snacks project), then Michael's e-mail announcing his school rock band, "The Rockers", its members and instruments, and its practice routine; the Present Continuous for actions happening now. *Lesson 2, "A weekend away!" (p. 62):* a holiday brochure for a Teen Camp offering unusual/extreme sports (white water rafting, scaling, abseiling, bungee jumping and others) alongside gentler options, a telephone conversation with the camp's manager/sports organiser, and the Present Continuous contrasted with the Present Simple for routine. *Lesson 3 (review lesson), "In my free time I learn English!" (p. 66):* a song about learning English through songs, comics, films and key pals; Magda's e-mail from a two-week exchange stay in Windsor (lessons, excursions to London, karaoke night); English–English dictionary skills (alphabetical order, stress, looking up meanings); pronunciation practice; and correcting a postcard using a teacher's writing-correction code. Project: a photo diary for a school trip. Self-assessment pp. 71–72, with a focus on writing strategies.

**Unit 6 — Bits and Pieces! (printed pp. 73–90).** Three lessons. *Lesson 1, "FOODstuff!" (p. 74):* a healthy-eating quiz with scored advice, food-and-snacks vocabulary sorted into "OK" and "be careful" groups, food collocations with *a slice/carton/packet/tin of*, countable and uncountable nouns with *a lot of / much / many* and *how much / how many*, the Food Guide Pyramid, and *should / shouldn't* advice used in a healthy-eating leaflet; project: a class survey on whether "our diet" is healthy. *Lesson 2, "TEEN Voice!" (p. 79):* a web poll, "School Uniforms: Love or Hate?", with short entries from pupils in several countries arguing for and against uniforms on cost, comfort and individuality grounds; clothes-and-accessories vocabulary; plural nouns including always-plural clothing words; comparatives used to judge which of two items is ideal for school. *Lesson 3, "The four corners of the Earth!" (p. 84):* a geography project text built entirely on superlatives — the Pacific as the largest ocean, the Nile as the longest river, the Mariana Trench, Everest, the Dead Sea, the Amazon and Angel Falls — with large numbers and geographical vocabulary; the superlative form, and *the* vs zero article with names of seas, rivers, lakes, mountains and waterfalls; writing is a short article about the UK using the appendix map. Self-assessment pp. 89–90.

**Unit 7 — In Our Mind's Eye! (printed pp. 91–108).** Three lessons; the Past Simple unit, the book's only past-tense unit. *Lesson 1, "Let's communic8!" (p. 92):* communication by people who cannot see, hear or speak, opened by the blind comics hero Daredevil and three short film recommendations from e-friends; an article adapted from the American Foundation for the Blind's Braille Bug site explains the six-dot Braille cell, how fast Braille readers read, and Louis Braille's life — blinded by an accident at three, inventor of the code at fifteen; learners write their names and a secret message in Braille. Vocabulary: punctuation marks and disability words. Grammar: *be* in the Past Simple, applied to famous people of the past (Einstein, John Lennon, Marie Curie, Agatha Christie and others). *Lesson 2, "Houston, we're back!" (p. 97):* Antonio's space e-mail, then a narrative article on Apollo 11 — the 20 July 1969 Moon landing, the lunar module "Eagle", about three hours on the surface collecting rocks and planting the flag, and the Pacific splashdown on 24 July; planet names and a planets quiz (key on p. 131, still counting nine planets including Pluto); listening news items on the Challenger, Columbia and Discovery shuttles; regular Past Simple forms, then a group press-style presentation of the mission. *Lesson 3, "TEEN best-sellers!" (p. 103):* a quiz matching classic authors to their books, then interviews with two living children's authors — Jacqueline Wilson, who became a writer at 17, and Antony Horowitz, whose Alex Rider hero was modelled on James Bond and whose first *Stormbreaker* took about a year to write; irregular Past Simple forms collected from the interviews; writing is a personal "life line" of important events. Self-assessment pp. 107–108, with a focus on listening strategies.

**Unit 8 — Tomorrow and … Beyond! (printed pp. 109–126).** Three lessons on the future, reworking the Advanced book's future unit at this lower level. *Lesson 1, "Travel Plans!" (p. 110):* Daphne from Patmos telephones an English friend about her July summer course — London and Cambridge, museums, Thorpe Park, punting — heard only on audio; travelling vocabulary grouped by airport, hotel and underground; ordinal numbers and dates; and the Present Continuous for fixed future arrangements, practised through a find-the-differences task on two teenagers' diaries. *Lesson 2, "Good for you!" (p. 115):* bad habits and advice, road-safety sentences recycling *must* and *can*, a radio phone-in of teenagers announcing this month's good intentions, *be going to* for plans and intentions (explicitly contrasted with the Present Continuous for fixed arrangements), and an anonymous diary entry about an upcoming party used as a writing model; project: planning the next school trip. *Lesson 3, "In the year 2525!" (p. 119):* learners brainstorm future life, then read a student article (credited as adapted from National Geographic Kids) predicting Personal Station taxis, domed cities with no pollution, thought-controlled machines and virtual-reality entertainment; the Future Simple (*will / won't*) for prediction; star-sign vocabulary, an online poll of teenagers' attitudes to horoscopes, a Greek-to-English mediation task retelling a magazine horoscope, and writing a magazine horoscope for a famous person. Self-assessment pp. 125–126, with a focus on learning new grammar.

**Unit 9 (Review) — It's a Masterpiece! (printed pp. 127–130).** A single review unit on art, replacing the Advanced book's summer-camp review. An e-project announcement invites teenagers to send in a favourite painting; learners match three pupils' comments to paintings, then listen to recorded e-gallery information and complete notes on works including Georgios Jakovides' *Children's Concert*, Georges Seurat's *A Sunday Afternoon on La Grande Jatte*, Gloria Ip Tung's *Work with others to save the Earth*, Eric Wu's *Futuristic City* and an unknown painter's *A Lady Listening to Music*, building a word bank for each. The project is to write, draft and display a short story behind a favourite painting, with Vermeer's *Girl with a Pearl Earring* and the Tracy Chevalier novel it inspired given as the model example.

**Appendices (printed pp. 131–204).** Quiz Key (p. 131: answers to the Unit 3 Australia quiz, the Unit 4 animal quiz, the Unit 7 planets and best-sellers quizzes, plus culture-corner notes and the Unit 9 art key); Speaking Appendix (pp. 132–141: paired Student A/B information-gap pages keyed to lessons, including the horoscope mediation texts in Greek); Maps (pp. 142–144: world map, map of the UK, and a map of the centre of Athens, largely pictorial); Grammar Appendix (pp. 145–157: full form/use tables following the course spine in order — *be* present, plural nouns, Present Simple and frequency adverbs, Wh-questions, imperatives and *if*-sentences, *can / can't*, *must / mustn't*, Present Continuous and its contrast with the Present Simple, *should* for advice, comparatives and superlatives, *the* / zero article, *be* and regular/irregular verbs in the Past Simple, Present Continuous for future arrangements, *be going to*, and the Future Simple); Self-Assessment Key (pp. 158–159); "It's Up to You!" (pp. 160–198: optional extra tasks numbered to match the main-book tasks they extend); Sources of texts and photographs (pp. 199–202, in Greek); a blank page (p. 203); and a legal/distribution notice (p. 204) stating the book is printed by ITYE–Diophantos under Law 3966/2011.

**Grammar spine as it arrives (summary):** Wh-questions + *be* + *there is / are* (U1) → *be*, *have got*, adjective order, *some / any*, prepositions of place, plural nouns (U2) → Present Simple, frequency adverbs, *like / love / enjoy / hate* + *-ing*, Wh-questions (U3) → imperative, *if* + present, *can / can't*, *must / mustn't* (U4) → Present Continuous vs Present Simple (U5) → countable/uncountable nouns and quantity, *should*, comparatives and superlatives, *the* / zero article (U6) → Past Simple (*be*, regular and irregular verbs) (U7) → ordinal numbers, Present Continuous for arrangements, *be going to*, Future Simple (U8) → whole-course review (U9).

### Honest negatives

- **No publication year is printed** on the cover, title page or imprint pages; only the "revised edition" stamp, the reissue note and in-file production dates (2015/2016, cover file 2023) are present. Any catalogue year for this book comes from outside the book itself.
- **Listening content cannot be verified from the PDF alone:** many tasks depend on audio (the Unit 2 collections listening on p. 13, the Unit 5 camp telephone call, the Unit 7 "Who is who" famous-people quiz on p. 96, the Unit 8 trip conversation and good-intentions phone-in, and the Unit 9 e-gallery recordings whose notes on p. 129 are blank listening gaps). Where a listening text is not printed in the book, this draft describes the task, not the audio's content.
- **A few pages are image-only or blank in the text layer** (cover spread, the maps on printed pp. 142–144, PDF p. 5, and the blank pages at printed pp. 198 and 203); their content is described from the rendered pages and contents listing, not from extracted text. On some heavily illustrated pages (e.g. printed pp. 46, 50, 66, 79, 84, 127) the text layer interleaves columns, so those summaries rest on the headings, tasks and Contents as well as the readable text.
- The book contains **no alphabet/phonics section and no separate pronunciation strand** in the Student's Book; pronunciation work exists only as short embedded links inside lessons.
- Dated content is part of the book as printed: the solar system is presented with nine planets including Pluto (printed p. 99), the zoo guidebook source is from 2001, the Lemony Snicket extract is credited to a 2005 edition, the horoscope mediation texts are adapted from a 2006 Greek teen magazine, and several web addresses and prices belong to that period, not the present day.
## Grade 7 (Beginners) — Teacher's Book

### Identity block

- **Real title as printed:** *Think Teen!* — "1st Grade of Junior High School / TEACHER'S BOOK", with the stream word **Αρχάριοι** (Beginners) printed on the front cover (bottom right, and on the spine), on the title page (PDF p. 2), and again on the imprint title page (PDF p. 4). Α΄ Γυμνασίου is the first year of Greek junior high school, i.e. Grade 7. The Greek record title "Αγγλικά Α΄ Γυμνασίου – Βιβλίο Εκπαιδευτικού" (English, 1st Grade of Gymnasio – Teacher's Book) matches this book.
- **Stream verdict:** BEGINNERS — confirmed. This is **not** the Advanced (Προχωρημένοι) teacher's book: every stream marker in this file reads Αρχάριοι, the book code and ISBN differ from the Advanced book's, and the teaching sequence inside is the beginners sequence (see the grammar order below, which reaches the Past Simple only in Unit 7).
- **Authors:** Ευαγγελία Καραγιάννη (Evangelia Karagianni), Βασιλική Κουή (Vasiliki / "Vicky" Koui), Αικατερίνη Νικολάκη (Aikaterini / "Katerina" Nikolaki) — named in Greek on the front cover and on both imprint pages (PDF pp. 3–4).

  - All page references below are printed pages unless a PDF page is stated.

### What the guide adds (own words; printed page references)

This is the teacher's companion to the Beginners *Think Teen!* Student's Book, Workbook and Audio CD. It does not reprint the pupil book; it tells the teacher how to run it, what the answers are, what to say and play, and how to test. Its added value falls into five blocks.

**1. A long method introduction (printed pp. ii–xviii).** The opening pages set out the design of the series: it is built on the Common European Framework of Reference (2001) and the Greek Cross-curricular Unified Framework (2003), develops all four skills through authentic and semi-authentic texts, and is explicitly designed both for pupils who had four years of primary English and for absolute beginners entering junior high school (p. ii). The components of the series and the anatomy of a unit — cover page, three lessons, project, end-of-unit test, can-do statements and a focus on learning strategies — are explained on p. iii. The rest of the introduction is a practical handbook, one section per skill or technique: how vocabulary is presented in thematic sets, through pictures, collocations and memory games, with extra games supplied (vocabulary notebooks, hangman, chain, bingo, learner-made crosswords; pp. iv–vi); how the Grammar Link works inductively, with pupils completing tables from input texts and checking themselves against the Grammar Appendix (p. vii); reading taught in a pre- / while- / post-reading frame and texts treated as vehicles of information rather than as language specimens (p. vii); listening with semi-scripted texts containing hesitations and rephrasing, worked through grids and tables so pupils need not rely on memory (p. viii); speaking moving from controlled to freer practice, with the teacher told to protect fluency, not to correct during the task, and to collect errors discreetly for a feedback slot afterwards (pp. viii–ix); pronunciation centred on stress and intonation and practised by choral repetition rather than individual reading aloud (p. ix); and writing taught as a process — brainstorming, several drafts, peer comment against criteria checklists, and a simple correction code (pp. ix–x). Further sections supply more games (Twenty Questions, Tell-the-Time Bingo, Noughts and Crosses, Tennis; pp. x–xii), class surveys, cross-curricular discussion topics, and a worked model for running projects with assigned roles, including roles a weaker pupil can succeed in (pp. xii–xiii). Assessment is formative throughout: a self-assessment at the end of every unit, can-do checklists, a learning-strategies focus that changes from unit to unit, and pupil portfolios (pp. xiii–xv). Differentiation is treated as built into the course rather than bolted on: the colour-coded "It's Up to You!" tasks offer a less demanding (green) and a more demanding (yellow) version of the same task, and pupils are trained to choose (pp. xv–xvi). The introduction closes with notes on the linked e-yliko CD for the beginners level, on when and how to use and correct the Workbook, a legend explaining the symbols used in the lesson plans, and a short reference list (pp. xvi–xviii).

**2. Step-by-step per-unit notes (printed pp. 1–117).** Each unit opens with a one-page planning table that no pupil book provides: the language functions, vocabulary link, grammar link, links to other school subjects and cross-curricular themes, the suggested lesson schedule in teaching periods, and an "Aids" list of things to bring (flashcards, maps, dictionaries, photographs, a large clock, recycling leaflets, and so on). The notes then walk through every task of the Student's Book in order, in a fixed pattern: aims and objectives, the vocabulary and structures to expect, a warm-up, the procedure, the answers, the tapescript where the task is a listening, pointers to the matching Workbook tasks, and frequent extras, background notes and "next lesson" preparation reminders. The nine units, with the grammar the guide actually teaches in each, are:

- **Unit 1 — Welcome! (pp. 1–8).** A single settling-in unit over four teaching periods: names and countries, presenting oneself and a partner, colours, classroom language and classroom objects, numbers, and favourite animals, hobbies and kinds of music. There is no new grammar presentation; the work is oral and lexical, with a Culture Corner and a project, and aids as concrete as colour flashcards and English–Greek dictionaries.
- **Unit 2 — All about us! (pp. 9–24).** *Lesson 1, "Hello there!":* personal information, sports, countries, nationalities, languages, family and school subjects; grammar is the Simple Present of *be*. *Lesson 2, "A collection of thimbles!":* favourite things and describing a room; *have got* and the order of adjectives of opinion, size, age, colour and material. *Lesson 3, "Feel at home!":* places and buildings in a neighbourhood; plural nouns, *there is / are*, *some / any* and prepositions of place. The guide adds, among much else, a background note on the painter Yannis Migadis, whose atelier picture is used for the room description (p. 18).
- **Unit 3 — Day in Day out! (pp. 25–40).** *Lesson 1, "My day!":* daily routines, leisure and telling the time; the Present Simple for *I / you / we / they* and adverbs of frequency. *Lesson 2, "Greetings from Australia!":* school subjects and likes; the Present Simple for *he / she / it* and *like / love / enjoy / hate* + verb-*ing*, with background on Australian schooling, including lessons broadcast "on air" (printed p. 33). *Lesson 3, "This is my job!":* jobs and work routines, idioms with *work*, and Wh- questions; the background notes even identify the lesson's job photographs, including Leonardo DiCaprio in *The Aviator* (printed p. 37).
- **Unit 4 — Ecofriendly! (pp. 41–54).** *Lesson 1, "Let's go to the zoo!":* instructions and advice through the imperative and *if*-sentences used for advice. *Lesson 2, "In the wild!":* animals, their habits and abilities; *can / can't* for ability. *Lesson 3, "Let's go green!"* (titled "We can make a difference!" in the unit table): recycling and protecting the environment; *must / mustn't* for obligation and prohibition. The notes supply animal-fact websites (including panda.org and the London Zoo site, printed p. 48) and extra poster and project support.
- **Unit 5 — Teens in action! (pp. 55–70).** *Lesson 1, "It's on the notice board!":* musical instruments and *play* collocations; the Present Continuous for actions happening now. *Lesson 2, "A weekend away!":* unusual sports; the Present Continuous contrasted with the Present Simple. *Lesson 3 is a review lesson, "In my free time I learn English!",* built on dictionary skills and the European Language Portfolio — the notes explain the Language Biography and its A1 self-assessment pages (printed p. 69).
- **Unit 6 — Bits and pieces! (pp. 71–84).** *Lesson 1, "FOODstuff!":* food, snacks and eating habits; countable and uncountable nouns with *a lot of / much / many* and *how much / how many*. *Lesson 2, "TEEN Voice!":* clothes and accessories; the comparative form of adjectives, with a class survey presented as a pie graph. *Lesson 3, "The four corners of the Earth!":* geographical words and large numbers; the superlative form and the definite / zero article. A radio quiz tapescript printed in the notes has the Pacific Ocean deeper than the Atlantic and Mount Everest as the highest mountain (printed p. 82).
- **Unit 7 — In our mind's eye! (pp. 85–98).** The past-tense unit, held back until here in the beginners stream. *Lesson 1, "Let's communic8!":* famous people of the past, physical problems and punctuation marks; the Simple Past of *be*. *Lesson 2, "Houston, we're back!":* space and the planets, narrating past events; the Simple Past of regular verbs, with background on the Apollo astronauts, Neil Armstrong named as commander of Apollo 11 (printed p. 91). *Lesson 3, "TEEN best-sellers!":* interviews with two popular authors and book vocabulary; the Simple Past of irregular verbs, and a "life line" speaking task (printed p. 98).
- **Unit 8 — Tomorrow and … beyond! (pp. 99–112).** *Lesson 1, "Travel plans!":* ordinal numbers and the Present Continuous used for future plans and arrangements; the cover-page notes identify the Adelphi Theatre, where *Evita* was on, in the London pictures (printed p. 100). *Lesson 2, "Good for you!":* bad habits and good intentions; *be going to* for future plans and intentions. *Lesson 3, "In the year 2525!":* predictions about future life and star signs; the Future Simple for predictions, plus a Culture Corner on the Chinese horoscope (printed p. 111).
- **Unit 9 (Review) — It's a masterpiece! (pp. 113–117).** A short review unit on paintings and painters, for two (or three) teaching periods: describing paintings, drawing conclusions and expressing opinions, feelings and preferences, with an IT-linked project researching painters. The guide prints a background story of Vermeer's *Girl With a Pearl Earring* — the maid Griet, aged 16 — for the teacher to use (printed p. 117).

Throughout the lesson notes the same kinds of teacher-only material recur: short cultural and factual background briefings (the Catalan painter Joan Miró, 1893 Barcelona – 1983 Majorca, behind the colours work, printed p. 5; Pierre-Auguste Renoir among the animal / art links, printed p. 46), web addresses to check before recommending them to pupils, "EXTRA!" alternative and extension tasks (games, peer correction, posters, a school band, London sights), and pronunciation support with printed tapescripts for the drills — down to the /s/–/ʃ/ tongue-twister on sea shells (printed p. 18).

**3. Answer keys.** Answers are given inside the lesson notes, task by task, as each task is taught, rather than gathered in one place — including suggested and possible answers where a task is open. Two gathered keys are then printed in the appendices: the key to the Student's Book's differentiated "It's Up to You!" tasks (printed pp. 145–148) and a full Workbook key (printed pp. 149–168), which runs unit by unit to the very end of the book, closing with Future Simple forms (printed p. 168).

**4. Audioscripts.** There is no single audioscript appendix for the Student's Book: the script of each listening is printed in the lesson notes at the point where it is taught, headed "Tapescript". They are complete enough to teach from without the CD in hand — for example the Unit 2 listening in which John describes his three-month-old puppy Woofy (printed p. 14) and the Unit 5 sentence-stress drill built on one sentence about Molly going to the theatre (printed p. 69). Separately, the scripts of the *test* listenings alone are gathered in the appendices (printed pp. 143–144; see below).

**5. Tests and marking support (printed pp. 118–144).** The appendices open with three photocopiable review tests, each covering all four skills and scored out of 100: Units 1–3 (pp. 118–121, opening with Tina's diary, dated Sunday, 19 October), Units 4–6 (pp. 122–127) and Units 7–9 (pp. 128–131). Paired speaking-task cards for the three test blocks follow (pp. 132–134). Then come the test keys (pp. 135–140), a sample rating scale for speaking tasks in tests (p. 141) and one for writing tasks (p. 142) — the speaking scale is a five-band scale across accuracy, fluency and pronunciation / intonation, with instructions for converting the band to a score out of 10, 15 or 20 — and finally the listening test tapescripts for all three blocks (pp. 143–144).

### Honest negatives

- **No publication year is printed** anywhere on the cover, title or imprint pages; only the November 2008 production slugs and the PDF creation date date the file. Any catalogue year for this edition comes from outside the book.
- **The audio itself cannot be verified from this PDF.** The guide prints tapescripts for the listenings at the point of use and for the test listenings in the appendices, but no CD is included in the file, so nothing here proves what the recordings sound like, how long they are, or whether every Student's Book listening has a script in the notes.
- **This guide cannot be quoted for the pupil texts themselves.** It paraphrases, answers and scripts the Student's Book tasks; the readings, dialogues and artwork the pupils see are in the Student's Book, not reproduced here, except where a tapescript or a test (printed pp. 118–131) prints a text in full.
- **Pagination is irregular and must not be flattened into one offset:** a blank page and an "Appendices" divider sit between the body and the tests (PDF pp. 142–143), the divider's own slug (119) is out of sequence with the test pages that follow it (118 onward), the Contents page is duplicated by a blank page with the same slug (PDF pp. 6–7), and three blank pages and a Greek-only legal notice (PDF pp. 195–198) close the file before the cover is repeated.
- **Much of the Greek front matter does not extract cleanly** (the credits page, PDF p. 3, uses a legacy Greek encoding), so names and roles on that page were read from the rendered page, not from the text layer; the legal notice on PDF p. 198 is likewise described from its rendered / slug evidence, not translated in full.
- The web addresses the guide recommends are printed as of the book's production (2008-era addresses, including an Encarta encyclopedia address on printed p. 5); this draft records that they are in the book and does not claim any of them is still live.
## Grade 7 (Beginners) — Workbook

### Identity block

- **Real title as printed:** *Think Teen!* — "1st Grade of Junior High School / WORKBOOK", with the stream word **Αρχάριοι** (Beginners) printed in white script on the front cover and on the spine, in red on the title page (PDF p. 2), and in grey on the imprint title page (PDF p. 4). The Greek catalogue title is "Αγγλικά Α΄ Γυμνασίου – Επίπεδο Αρχαρίων – Τετράδιο Εργασιών" (English, 1st Grade of Gymnasio – Beginners Level – Workbook). Α΄ Γυμνασίου is the first year of Greek junior high school, i.e. Grade 7.
- **Stream verdict:** BEGINNERS — confirmed. This is **not** the Advanced (Προχωρημένοι) book. The word Αρχάριοι appears on the cover, spine, title page and imprint title page.
- **Authors:** Ευαγγελία Καραγιάννη (Evangelia Karagianni), Βασιλική Κουή (Vasiliki Koui), Αικατερίνη Νικολάκη (Aikaterini Nikolaki) — the same team as the Student's Book. Writing contractor named on the imprint title page: Ελληνικά Γράμματα (Ellinika Grammata), under the auspices of the Pedagogical Institute.
- **Publisher:** Ινστιτούτο Τεχνολογίας Υπολογιστών και Εκδόσεων «ΔΙΟΦΑΝΤΟΣ» (Institute of Computer Technology and Publications "Diophantos" — ITYE Diophantos), for the Υπουργείο Παιδείας, Θρησκευμάτων και Αθλητισμού (Ministry of Education, Religions and Sports) / Ινστιτούτο Εκπαιδευτικής Πολιτικής (Institute of Educational Policy). Distributed via ebooks.edu.gr.
- **ISBN:** 978-960-06-2682-7 (printed on the back cover). **Book code:** 0-21-0045 (back cover barcode element: (01) 000000 0 21 0045 6). This matches the manifest record for this file (21-0045-02, Tetradio Ergasion, Beginners).
- **Edition / year:** No calendar year is printed on the cover, title or imprint pages. The imprint page (PDF p. 3) states the reissue was produced by ITYE Diophantos from a digital mockup funded under ESPA / "ΣΤΗΡΙΖΩ", with corrections approved by the Institute of Educational Policy. In-file production stamps differ by signature (2014, 2015, 2023 and 2024 dates all appear in the page slugs). No year is asserted beyond what is printed/stamped.
- **Extent:** 162 PDF pages; 155 printed pages plus unnumbered front matter and cover spreads. Printed pp. 1–113 are the nine units, printed pp. 114–147 are the appendix, printed p. 148 is blank, printed pp. 149–154 are the sources and legal pages (with blanks among them).
- **Page offset:** **printed page = PDF page − 7** throughout the numbered body, appendix and sources (e.g. printed p. 1 = PDF p. 8; printed p. 66 = PDF p. 73; printed p. 149 = PDF p. 156). PDF pp. 1–4 are the cover spread, title page and imprint pages; PDF p. 5 is blank; PDF pp. 6–7 are the Contents; PDF p. 162 repeats the cover spread.
- **How the workbook is built (read this first):** The workbook mirrors the Beginners Student's Book unit for unit and lesson for lesson — same nine unit titles and same lesson titles throughout — but in compressed form and with its own readings and exercises. Nearly every main task carries a cross-reference of the form "Task N – p. 114" pointing to a parallel, more heavily scaffolded version of the same task in the closing appendix, "It's up to you!" (Tasks 1–60). Tasks throughout are star-rated for difficulty (one to three stars). There is no listening strand and no answer key in this book; the work is Reading, Vocabulary Link, Grammar Link and Writing only.

### Unit-by-unit summary (own words; printed page references)

**Unit 1 — Welcome! (printed pp. 1–6).** A single opening lesson, with no grammar section. Reading (p. 2) is three short self-profiles — a girl from England, a boy from Brazil who goes by a short form of his name, and a Greek boy — and learners pick names out of statements about age, country, surname, favourite colour, sport and hobby. Vocabulary work covers English words that also appear on Greek signs (with a dictionary hunt for true Greek equivalents), school objects and colours through "What's this?" questions, numbers drilled as little arithmetic puzzles whose answers are number words, and a word-snake that has to be sorted into animals and hobbies. Writing (p. 6) is a personal profile card for joining an e-group: name, age, country, favourite colour, number, animal and hobby.

**Unit 2 — All about us! (printed pp. 7–20).** Three lessons. *Lesson 1, "Hello, there!" (p. 8):* a teenager in Oxford e-mails new keypals about herself, her school and her two contrasting friends; learners circle referents, correct false statements, sort sports words with missing letters, group nationalities by their endings (-an / -ese / -ish / other), and then work through full form tables for the verb *be* in affirmative, negative, interrogative and short answers before writing an introductory e-mail with a chosen opening and closing. *Lesson 2, "A collection of thimbles!" (p. 13):* Guinness World Records extracts about four outsized collections (neck ties, bags, mugs, model cars) with record cards to complete; vocabulary is collection words and adjectives sorted into opinion / size / age / colour / material columns — the adjective-order point is then used in the writing task, an e-mail to the Guinness site about the learner's own collection. Grammar is *have got* in full tables. *Lesson 3, "Feel at home!" (p. 17):* neighbourhood signs matched to places, a gap-fill article about London, building words, plural-noun spelling rules (including the irregulars and the -o exceptions), *there is / there are*, *a / an / some / any*, and prepositions of place practised inside a girl's description of her neighbourhood in Sparti, which is also the model for the writing.

**Unit 3 — Day in Day out! (printed pp. 21–34).** Three lessons; the Present Simple unit. *Lesson 1, "My day!" (p. 22):* a schoolgirl's weekday routine (alarm, bus, lessons, lunch at home, martial-arts days, homework, a late bedtime) is sequenced against pictures; vocabulary is telling the time and routine collocations sorted by odd-one-out; grammar presents the Present Simple for *I / you / we / they* with adverbs of frequency and time expressions. *Lesson 2, "Greetings from Australia!" (p. 26):* four short "a day in the life of…" magazine texts (an office worker, a mother, a small child, a retired man) are matched to pictures and questioned; a wordsearch hides ten school subjects; grammar completes the Present Simple with the third person (-s / -es / -ies spelling rules); writing is the learner's own school timetable plus an e-mail about their school week. *Lesson 3, "This is my job!" (p. 31):* five first-person job descriptions (doctor, waiter/waitress, clerk, clothes designer, architect) are matched to names and pictures; a jobs crossword, workplaces spidergrams and four idioms with *work* follow; grammar is wh-questions, and the writing task is a guess-my-job paragraph that withholds the job name for a partner to identify.

**Unit 4 — Ecofriendly! (printed pp. 35–48).** Three lessons. *Lesson 1, "Let's go to the zoo!" (p. 36):* weekend advertisements (city park, shopping centre, cinema offer, Potter films advert) are matched to families' stated wishes; zoo signs and notices and zoo collocations follow; grammar is the imperative and first if-sentences of the form *if + Present Simple → imperative / can*; writing is a paragraph of suggestions for a partner's free weekend. *Lesson 2, "In the wild!" (p. 40):* five zoo-guidebook animal descriptions (zebra, elephant, tiger, panda, shark, with heights and weights) are matched to photos; vocabulary sorts animals, habitats, food and body parts and practises animal-ability collocations; grammar is *can / can't* for ability in full tables, plus a short opinion dialogue to complete from the Student's Book language bank; writing is a school-newspaper article about a favourite animal on a given frame. *Lesson 3, "Let's go green!" (p. 45):* a children's article on global warming adapted from the US EPA site lists six everyday actions (carpooling, switching off, low-energy products, walking/cycling/bus, planting trees, solar energy); vocabulary is recycling sorting and environment collocations; grammar is *must / mustn't*, applied first to "Green Rules" and classroom rules and finally to an e-mail of green advice to a Spanish school eco-team.

**Unit 5 — Teens in action! (printed pp. 49–64).** Three lessons; the Present Continuous unit. *Lesson 1, "It's on the notice board!" (p. 50):* four short notes pinned up at school are matched to clubs (sports, eco, drawing, photography, cookery), with a reference-words task; club vocabulary and collocations follow; grammar presents the Present Continuous with the -ing spelling rules (drop -e, double consonant, keep -y); writing is an e-mail describing photos of the learner's own school clubs. *Lesson 2, "A weekend away!" (p. 55):* an Extreme Sports Camp advertisement with a full daily timetable is mined for facts; sports and activity collocations are matched and reused; grammar contrasts Present Continuous (now) with Present Simple (routines) through signal phrases, word-order and question-formation tasks; writing is an advertisement for the learner's own summer camp. *Lesson 3, "In my free time I learn English!" (Review, p. 60):* a learning-styles text sorts learners into visual, auditory and kinesthetic types with tick-box self-descriptions; then dictionary work (alphabetical order), a mixed crossword, collocations, a further Present Simple vs Continuous set, and an error-correction writing page where each mistake is labelled by type (spelling, word order, grammar, wrong tense, wrong word).

**Unit 6 — Bits and pieces! (printed pp. 65–78).** Three lessons. *Lesson 1, "FOODstuff!" (p. 66):* a teen health webpage in three extracts (food labels, whether teens should diet, ways to good health) adapted from a children's health site; food anagrams, container phrases (*a slice of, a carton of…*), and grammar on countable/uncountable nouns with *a lot of / much / many* and *how much / how many*; advice grammar *should / shouldn't* is practised as "Healthy Diet Rules" and then written as rules for the school canteen. *Lesson 2, "TEEN Voice!" (p. 70):* a fashion webpage with three links (tips, stories, a just-for-guys page) adapted from fashion sites; opposites, clothes and accessories vocabulary, the singular/plural split in clothes words, and the comparative (spelling rules, *more*, and the irregular *worse*); writing is a description-plus-comparison of two magazine models, set as a partner guessing task. *Lesson 3, "The four corners of the Earth!" (p. 75):* a travel-guide article on Dubai (sights, sport and leisure including an indoor ski run in the desert, shopping, a sail-shaped luxury hotel) is headed and questioned; geographical-features matching and large numbers in words follow; grammar is the superlative and the *the* / zero-article rules for geographical names; the writing is a tourist-information brochure about Greece, using a geography project in the Student's Book.

**Unit 7 — In our mind's eye! (printed pp. 79–92).** Three lessons; the Past Simple unit, taken in three passes. *Lesson 1, "Let's communic8!" (p. 80):* a magazine article explains emoticons as feeling-pictures built from keyboard characters, with a ten-item emoticon matching whose answers are printed small on the page; vocabulary is communication words and famous-people words (inventor, poet, queen, emperor…); grammar is the Past Simple of *be* and *there was / were*, reused in a report comparing the learner's primary school with their junior high school. *Lesson 2, "Houston, we're back!" (p. 85):* a solar-system quiz is checked against short planet texts (the Sun, Saturn, Mars, Mercury, Neptune, Uranus, Pluto); a space crossword and a planet-names list (English and Greek) follow; grammar is the Past Simple of regular verbs with all four spelling groups, then true-sentence correction about the Moon landing using the Student's Book account; writing is a "mission to space" story for a web competition. *Lesson 3, "TEEN best-sellers!" (p. 89):* the back cover of a comic-strip teen novel about a boy planning an escape from a changing family is read as a text in its own right (where would you find it, what is the title, who is who); book vocabulary (author, publisher, character, plot, paperback…) and collocations follow; grammar is the Past Simple of irregular verbs with a full verb list to convert; writing is an e-mail about what the learner did yesterday, built from a day's notes.

**Unit 8 — Tomorrow and … beyond! (printed pp. 93–108).** Three lessons; the future unit, also in three passes. *Lesson 1, "Travel plans!" (p. 94):* three holiday advertisements (singles-and-couples child-free holidays, activity holidays, family holidays with childcare) are matched to five sets of holidaymakers; travelling vocabulary is grouped by place (hotel, airport, underground) and dates are written out in words; grammar is the Present Continuous for fixed future arrangements, questioned through a boy's holiday plans; writing is an e-mail built from an advertisement for teen holidays on Greek islands. *Lesson 2, "Good for you!" (p. 99):* a webpage of ten New Year resolutions for teens (only six are printed in full) is matched to pictures — a workbook curiosity, since the page itself asks who the article is for and the text addresses parents about their teenagers; collocations about behaviour and safety follow; grammar is *be going to* for plans and intentions, contrasted with the Present Continuous for fixed plans, with an extra-word error hunt; there is no separate writing task in this lesson. *Lesson 3, "In the year 2525!" (p. 103):* a weekly teen horoscope for seven signs is read for detail; collocations and the twelve star signs with their dates follow; grammar is the Future Simple (*will / won't*) for prediction, practised on pictured characters and on the learner's own future; writing is a funny horoscope for a best friend, entered for a magazine competition.

**Unit 9 (Review) — It's a masterpiece! (printed pp. 109–113).** A five-page review with no new material: ten short extracts lifted from this workbook's own earlier readings (collections, a job, global warming, learning styles, diet, fashion, Dubai, emoticons, Saturn, the horoscope) are matched to their headings and voted on; vocabulary is revised as word groups and a choose-the-word quiz that recycles earlier collocation tasks almost verbatim; a twelve-sentence grammar review asks learners both to choose the correct form and to name the grammar point it illustrates; and a final writing page recycles ten extracts from the year's writing tasks and asks learners to complete them and name their genres (story, invitation, friendly letter, request, place description, timetable, job description, suggestions letter, advertisement, appearance description). The unit opener (p. 109) pictures the Beginners Student's Book cover itself.

**Appendix — "It's up to you!" (printed pp. 114–147).** Sixty numbered tasks, grouped by unit (Units 1–8; Unit 9 has none), each a second, more scaffolded pass at a task from the main workbook: the same readings return with underlining, key-word, first-letter and multiple-choice support, and the same grammar points return as choose-the-correct-form exercises. Workbook-only additions inside the appendix: Task 1 (p. 114) extends the Unit 1 profiles with a fourth child, a 14-year-old in Canada whose parents are from France and who loves ballet; Task 55 (pp. 143–144) adds a full months-and-ordinals set that has no counterpart task in the main lessons; and several appendix tasks split one main task into two (e.g. the travelling-vocabulary task returns as both Task 53, words supplied in boxes, and Task 54, picture labelling). The appendix is therefore not an answer key and not new teaching material — it is the same course at a lower step, and it is the single largest workbook-only component (34 printed pages).

**Back matter (printed pp. 148–154).** Printed p. 148 is blank. Printed p. 149 lists, in Greek, the sources of the workbook's texts (Guinness World Records site for the collections, the US EPA children's pages for global warming, a children's health site for the food article, fashion sites for the fashion webpage, Dubai information sites, an emoticons page, a children's astronomy site, the back cover of the Puffin novel for the book blurb, and a travel site and a parenting site for the holiday adverts and resolutions) — under a heading that, as printed, names the **Student's Book**, not the Workbook (see Honest negatives). Printed p. 151 lists photograph sources; printed pp. 150, 152 and 153 are blank; printed p. 154 is the standard legal/distribution notice stating the book is printed by ITYE–Diophantos under Law 3966/2011. PDF p. 162 repeats the cover spread.

**Grammar spine as it arrives (summary):** no grammar in U1 → *be*, *have got*, plurals, *there is/are*, *a/an/some/any*, place prepositions (U2) → Present Simple in two passes, frequency adverbs, wh-questions (U3) → imperative, if-sentences, *can/can't*, *must/mustn't* (U4) → Present Continuous, then Present Continuous vs Present Simple (U5) → countable/uncountable and quantifiers, *should/shouldn't*, comparative, superlative, *the*/zero article (U6) → Past Simple in three passes: *be* / *there was/were*, regular verbs, irregular verbs (U7) → future in three passes: Present Continuous for arrangements, *be going to*, Future Simple (U8) → whole-course review (U9).

### Honest negatives

- **No publication year is printed** on the cover, title page or imprint pages; only the reissue note and in-file production dates (2014/2015/2023/2024, varying by signature) are present. Any catalogue year for this book comes from outside the book itself.
- **There is no answer key and no self-assessment section** in this workbook, unlike the Student's Book: apart from the emoticon answers printed on printed p. 80 itself, no task in the main units or the appendix is keyed anywhere in the book.
- **There is no listening, speaking or pronunciation strand:** every unit opener lists only reading, vocabulary, grammar and writing work, and no task in the 162 PDF pages refers to audio. Any speaking is limited to partner-checking and acting out two short dialogues (printed p. 43).
- **The sources appendix is mislabelled as printed:** its heading (printed p. 149) names the Beginners *Student's Book* (Βιβλίο Μαθητή), not the Workbook, although the texts it sources are the workbook's own readings. It is reproduced here as found, not corrected.
- **Dated content is part of the book as printed:** Pluto is treated as a planet and the solar-system crossword speaks of nine planets (printed pp. 85–86); London is called the largest city in Europe with about 7.5 million people (printed p. 17); the Burj al-Arab is called the tallest hotel in the world (printed p. 75). These reflect the book's 2000s-era sources, not the present day.
- **Print errors stand as printed** and are not silently corrected above: "clerck" for clerk (printed p. 31), "PACTICE" on the Unit 4 opener (printed p. 35), a Student's Book reference to "page 1085" (printed p. 78), and "wiill" in appendix Task 60 (printed p. 147).
- **A few pages are blank or image-only in the text layer** (PDF p. 5; printed pp. 148, 150, 152, 153) and some pictorial pages extract in scrambled order (the advertisements on printed pp. 36 and 94 and the review extracts on printed p. 110); their content above is described from the rendered pages and the Contents, not from clean extracted text.
## Grade 7 — Glossaries (Advanced and Beginners)

Both files are the printable-form glossaries (Γλωσσάριο — Εκτυπώσιμη Μορφή) for *Think Teen!*, the Grade 7 (Α΄ Γυμνασίου) English course. Each is a companion to one stream of the Grade 7 Student's Book: the green-covered Advanced book (Προχωρημένοι) and the blue-covered Beginners book (Αρχάριοι). **Identity verdict for both files: MATCH** — cover, credits page, running heads and content all confirm the stream named in the record; no mismatch was found in either book (details and evidence below).

---

### Book 1 — Advanced Glossary

#### Identity block

- **Title as printed (cover, PDF p. 1):** ΑΓΓΛΙΚΑ — Α΄ Γυμνασίου - Προχωρημένοι, Γλωσσάρι; in English on the same cover: "Think Teen 1st Grade - Advanced Glossary". The cover reproduces the green *Think Teen! 1st Grade of Junior High School — STUDENT'S BOOK* cover marked Προχωρημένοι.
- **Publisher / imprint:** Ινστιτούτο Τεχνολογίας Υπολογιστών & Εκδόσεων «Διόφαντος» (ITYE "Diophantos" — Institute of Computer Technology and Publications), for the Υπουργείο Παιδείας και Θρησκευμάτων (ΥΠΑΙΘ, Ministry of Education and Religious Affairs), under the Ψηφιακό Σχολείο (Digital School) programme, ΕΣΠΑ 2007–2013 / EU co-funded (credits page, PDF p. 2).
- **Edition / year as printed:** Έκδοση 1.0 / Απρίλιος 2013 — "Version 1.0 / April 2013" (credits page, PDF p. 2). No other year is printed in the file.
- **ISBN:** None — no ISBN is printed on the cover or credits page, and the string "ISBN" does not occur anywhere in the file's text.
- **Credits as printed (PDF p. 2):** Development team (Ομάδα ανάπτυξης) of eleven named English teachers / e-learning and IT specialists (Eleni Argyriou, Katelis Vigklas, Georgia Gyftoula, Katerina Makri, Souzan Moutsouroufi, Antigoni Bratsoli, Sofia Mysirlaki, Katerina Nikolaki, Chrysanthi Sotiriou, Mairi Frentzou, Vasilis Chartzoulakis); digitisation by Ioannis Bitros; coordinator Vasiliki Mitsikopoulou, Associate Professor, EKPA. Licence: Creative Commons 3.0 / CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Produced within the project «Ψηφιακή Εκπαιδευτική Πλατφόρμα, Διαδραστικά Βιβλία και Αποθετήριο Μαθησιακών Αντικειμένων» (ebooks.edu.gr line).
- **Extent:** 67 PDF pages — PDF p. 1 = cover, PDF p. 2 = credits page, PDF pp. 3–67 = 65 pages of glossary tables.
- **Printed page numbers / offset:** **None — the content pages carry no printed folio numbers at all** (checked in the text layer of every page and visually on rendered pages). There is therefore no printed = PDF offset; all references below are to **PDF pages**. The cover itself (PDF p. 1) is an image-only page with no text layer.

#### How this glossary is organised (own words)

The whole book is one long set of tables, running from PDF p. 3 to PDF p. 67 with no contents page, no introduction and no index. The tables follow the Student's Book in order: a section headed "Unit 1" (2 pages), then, for Units 2–8, sections headed by Introduction (Units 4–8 only) and Lesson 1, Lesson 2 and Lesson 3, and finally a single undivided "Unit 9" section (2 pages). There are **no Self Assessment sections** in this stream's glossary. Every page carries the same six-column table — **Word | Definition | Example | Synonym | Antonym | Derived forms** — with alternate rows shaded grey and a running head naming the unit on the left and "Think Teen! A Γυμνασίου Προχωρημένοι" on the right.

Each entry gives the headword with a part-of-speech tag — (n), (v), (adj), (adv), (expr), (conj), (prep) — then a short definition in simple English with a Greek equivalent appended at the end of the definition, then one example sentence using the word. Synonyms, antonyms and derived (word-family) forms are given where the compilers had them; very many of those three cells are simply blank. There is **no phonetic transcription anywhere** in the book. Within a lesson section the entries run broadly A–Z (Unit 1, for example, opens "add up", "beef", "belong", "break the ice", "champion" and closes, on the next page, with "puppy" through "wrong"), though the order is the book's teaching order rather than a strict dictionary alphabet, and phrases and proper items sit inside the same runs.

Size and scope: counting part-of-speech tags in the text gives roughly **930 entries** — about 570 nouns, 185 verbs, 125 adjectives and some 50 adverbs, expressions and other items (an approximate count: a few headwords wrap across lines, so the true figure is "on the order of nine hundred"). The vocabulary is the full word-stock of the Advanced Student's Book, including topic sets such as food and sport in Unit 1, food/health words in Unit 3 (Lesson 1 opens with "additive", "alternative", "amount", "article"), travel words in Unit 5 (its Introduction opens with "contact", "culture", "departure", "destination") and outdoor-activity words in Unit 9 ("abseiling", "archery", "backgammon", "canoeing", "eco-holidays", "trekking").

Two short sample entries, quoted as fragments only: "add up (v)" is defined as putting numbers together to reach a total, with the Greek προσθέτω and derived forms "addition, additional"; "break the ice (expr)" is defined as making people who have not met feel relaxed, Greek σπάω τον πάγο, with an example about telling jokes when people first meet.

### Book 2 — Beginners Glossary

#### Identity block

- **Title as printed (cover, PDF p. 1):** ΑΓΓΛΙΚΑ — Α΄ Γυμνασίου - Αρχάριοι, Γλωσσάρι; in English on the same cover: "Think Teen 1st Grade - Beginners Glossary". The cover reproduces the blue *Think Teen! 1st Grade of Junior High School — STUDENT'S BOOK* cover marked Αρχάριοι.
- **Publisher / imprint:** ITYE "Diophantos" for the Ministry of Education and Religious Affairs (ΥΠΑΙΘ), Ψηφιακό Σχολείο (Digital School) programme, ΕΣΠΑ 2007–2013 / EU co-funded — identical imprint wording to the Advanced glossary (credits page, PDF p. 2).
- **Edition / year as printed:** Έκδοση 1.0 / Απρίλιος 2013 — "Version 1.0 / April 2013" (credits page, PDF p. 2).
- **ISBN:** None — no ISBN on cover or credits page, and "ISBN" does not occur anywhere in the file's text.
- **Credits as printed (PDF p. 2):** The credits page is identical to the Advanced one — the same eleven-person development team, the same digitiser (Ioannis Bitros) and the same coordinator (Vasiliki Mitsikopoulou, EKPA); CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 licence; same Digital Educational Platform project.
- **Extent:** 48 PDF pages — PDF p. 1 = cover, PDF p. 2 = credits page, PDF pp. 3–48 = the glossary tables.
- **Printed page numbers / offset:** The content pages **are** foliated: **printed page = PDF page − 2** throughout (printed p. 1 = PDF p. 3; printed p. 46 = PDF p. 48, the last page). References below give both numbers. As in the Advanced file, the cover (PDF p. 1) is image-only.

#### How this glossary is organised (own words)

The design is identical to the Advanced glossary — the same six columns (**Word | Definition | Example | Synonym | Antonym | Derived forms**), the same grey-shaded alternate rows, the same style of entry: headword with part-of-speech tag, a simple English definition with the Greek equivalent appended, and (for most entries) one example sentence; synonyms, antonyms and derived forms filled in only patchily, and again **no phonetics anywhere**. The running head reads "Think Teen! A Γυμνασίου Αρχάριοι".

The section structure differs from the Advanced book in three ways. First, it is finer-grained at the start of each unit: most units open with an "Introduction" section, and Units 2, 5 and 8 close with an extra "Self Assessment" section, which the Advanced glossary does not have at all. Second, Unit 1 is again a single undivided section, and its two pages show two alphabetical runs under the one heading (a first run from "agree" to "survey", and a second run beginning "bubble (speech bubble)", "dictionary", "e-friend" …), suggesting two sub-lists merged without a new heading; a similar second run of capitalised items (place names and school subjects — "Amsterdam", "Ankara", "Beijing", "Biology", "Canberra" …) appears inside Unit 2 – Lesson 1. Third, the book ends with a **Unit 9 – Lesson 1** section only (printed pp. 45–46): there is no Lesson 2 or Lesson 3 glossary for Unit 9 in this stream, and the final printed page holds just three entries ("science fiction", "vivid", "word of mouth").

Size and scope: roughly **675 entries** by the same part-of-speech-tag count (about 450 nouns, 120 adjectives, 80 verbs and some 25 phrases, phrasal verbs and others) over 46 printed pages — about two-thirds the size of the Advanced glossary, matching the smaller Beginners word-stock. The topics follow the Beginners Student's Book: Unit 2 – Introduction is everyday objects and school life ("belong", "brochure", "camera", "camp", "club", "concert", "thimble", "world"); Unit 7 – Introduction turns to space and people ("amazing", "astronaut", "blind", "favourite"); Unit 9 – Lesson 1 mixes art, media and the future ("accompany", "chewing gum", "exhibition", "futuristic", "masterpiece", "science fiction").

A short sample entry, quoted as a fragment: "thimble (n)" is defined as a small cup worn to protect the finger that pushes the needle through cloth when sewing, with the Greek δαχτυλήθρα.

### How the two glossaries differ (own words)

- **Size:** Advanced — 67 PDF pages, 65 of them tables, roughly 930 entries. Beginners — 48 PDF pages, 46 printed pages of tables, roughly 675 entries. The Advanced book is about a third larger again, in line with the two Student's Books.
- **Pagination:** Beginners content pages are numbered (printed = PDF − 2); Advanced content pages have no printed numbers at all, so Advanced can only be cited by PDF page.
- **Sections:** Both follow their Student's Book unit by unit and lesson by lesson, but Beginners adds Introduction sections more consistently and has Self Assessment sections for Units 2, 5 and 8; Advanced has no Self Assessment sections and no Introduction sections before Unit 4. Beginners' Unit 9 glossary covers Lesson 1 only; Advanced treats Unit 9 as one undivided section — and the two Unit 9 word sets are almost entirely different (Advanced: outdoor sports and travel; Beginners: art, media and the future), sharing little beyond "narrator" and "vivid".
- **Shared entries:** Many headwords occur in both books, and where they do, the treatment is often the same or nearly so — e.g. "narrator (n)" carries the identical example "In this book, the narrator is a teenager." in both, and "vivid (adj)" the identical example "That poster has many vivid colours."; the Beginners version of "vivid" gives the Greek έντονος, ζωηρός in its definition, where the Advanced version's definition is English-only ("bright and strong"), though the Advanced entry lists more synonyms and both derived forms ("vividly", "vividness"). Other shared words ("agree", "belong", "foreign", "scene") are independently worded in each book.
- **Everything else is common to both:** same publisher, credits, version and date (1.0, April 2013), same six-column layout, same definition-plus-Greek-equivalent entry style, same absence of phonetics, contents page and index.

### Honest negatives

- **No ISBN exists in either file** — neither on the covers nor anywhere in the text; these printable downloads were apparently never given one.
- **No phonetic transcription, no pronunciation guidance, no contents page, no introduction and no alphabetical index** in either glossary; a pupil can only find a word if they know which unit and lesson it came from.
- **The Advanced glossary has no printed page numbers**, so any citation to it must use PDF pages; the Beginners glossary is foliated but its cover and credits pages are unnumbered, hence the −2 offset.
- **Coverage gaps inside entries:** the Synonym, Antonym and Derived forms cells are blank for a large share of entries in both books, and a few entries lack even an example sentence (e.g. Beginners "e-programme (n)", printed p. 1, has a definition and Greek equivalent but no example).
- **Source errors preserved as printed:** Advanced has "coyntry" [sic] in the definition of "nationality" (PDF p. 3) and the headword "archaelogist" [sic] (PDF p. 37). In the Beginners file the "Amsterdam" headword on printed p. 4 (PDF p. 6) is rendered with garbled, overprinted characters in the source PDF itself, although its definition ("Amsterdam is a city of the Netherlands, Αμστερνταμ") is legible.
- **Entry counts are approximate:** they were obtained by counting part-of-speech tags in the extracted text; wrapped headwords and the two-run layout of Beginners Unit 1 mean the figures (~930 Advanced, ~675 Beginners) should be read as orders of magnitude, not exact censuses.
- The Beginners glossary simply stops after Unit 9 – Lesson 1 (printed p. 46, three entries); whether the Beginners Student's Book has further Unit 9 lessons cannot be settled from this glossary alone.
## Grade 8 (Advanced) — Student's Book — *Think Teen! 2nd Grade of Junior High School, Student's Book (Προχωρημένοι)*

### Identity block

- **Real title as printed:** *Think Teen!* — "2nd Grade of Junior High School / STUDENT'S BOOK", with the stream word **Προχωρημένοι** (Advanced) printed in a yellow jigsaw piece on the front cover and in brackets, as ΠΡΟΧΩΡΗΜΕΝΟΙ, under "STUDENT'S BOOK" on both title pages. Β΄ ΓΥΜΝΑΣΙΟΥ (2nd Grade of Gymnasio) is the second year of Greek junior high school, i.e. Grade 8.
- **Stream verdict:** ADVANCED — confirmed. This is **not** the Beginners (αρχαρίων) book. The Advanced word appears on the cover, on the title page (PDF p. 2) and on the full imprint title page (PDF p. 4).
